384YE Winter Solstice Conclave sessions.d: Precedence went to the Unfettered Mind, with 335 mana distributed among the orders. The Conclave asked for a title to identify sorcerers, told the magistrates that interdicted Urizen lore was illegal to cast but not to learn or teach, and sent the Silver Chalice to Madruga's thirsty grasses. The Flower is Withered on the Stalk and Fire on the Water were added to Imperial lore. The Conclave also endowed Sadogua to help persecuted Iron Confederacy mages flee, welcomed Suranni refugees, approved Claude Videre as a Throne candidate and asked the Rod and Shield to deal with creatures in Metri. Proposals on vigilance, interdicting the potion of bone dust and a Seventh Mist base in Redoubt failed.

n.Urizen: The Conclave told the magistrates that interdicted rituals from Urizen lore should be treated like Imperial lore: illegal to cast but lawful to learn and teach. Their texts, including those in the Grand Library of Canterspire, are not to be seized or destroyed. A separate bid to back a Seventh Mist research base in the Brilliant Star in Redoubt failed.
n.Wintermark: Speaking for the Winterfolk, Aethalstan Korping secured Conclave's agreement that the Shuttered Lantern should investigate blood-on-the-snow cultists tied to Agramant in Sermersuaq.

t.Sermersuaq: Conclave backed the Shuttered Lantern in investigating blood-on-the-snow cultists and tearing the veil on the Voice in the Pines' activities in Sermersuaq. The outcome is recorded in the Anyone but you Wind of Fortune.

384YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: Senators were chosen for Astolat, Hercynia (twice), Kallavesa, Madruga, Miekarova, Necropolis, Ossium, Skarsind, Temeschwar and Zenith. The Senate appointed four ambassadors, including Abel to the Grendel, and ten generals, among them Aracelis I Erigo of the Burning Falcon and Skywise Rykana of the Winter Sun. It also filled numerous sinecures such as the Grimnir of Wittal Grove. The Synod raised Darian Numbers as Cardinal of Prosperity with 253 votes and Hywel Summer Crow as Cardinal of the Way. Bourse auctions included the Hunt of Alderei the Fair, which went for 575 thrones. Andronikos of the Lighthouse at Nikephoros declared candidacy for Warmage, and Aitana i Riqueza became Prefect of the Conclave.

n.Dawn: Cecilia De Gauvain was elected Senator for Astolat, giving Dawn's territory its voice in the Senate.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Abel was appointed by the Senate as the Empire's Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Eli of the Cenotaph was elected Senator for Necropolis, representing Highguard's territory in the Senate.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected Senator for Skarsind, and RAKK won the Bourse vote for Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
n.Navarr: Hercynia held two senatorial elections this summit, with Rhisiart Dancewalker the most recent winner after Gelert Ashborn.
n.The Brass Coast: Chiara Zayden Riqueza was elected Senator for Madruga, representing the Brass Coast territory in the Senate.
n.The League: Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar was elected Senator for Temeschwar, the League territory.
n.Urizen: Cadeus was elected Senator for Zenith, giving Urizen's territory its representative in the Senate.
n.Varushka: Varushka chose two senators: Talvikaarne, The Winter Guest, for Miekarova, and Vesna (Sparrow) Borkovna for Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Rane Shardbearer was elected Senator for Kallavesa, and Branwynn Rynne was appointed Grimnir of Wittal Grove within that territory.

t.Astolat: Cecilia De Gauvain became Astolat's senator.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia held two senatorial elections at this summit, and Rhisiart Dancewalker, the most recent winner, took the seat after Gelert Ashborn.
t.Kallavesa: Rane Shardbearer was elected Senator for Kallavesa, and the territory's Grimnir of Wittal Grove title went to Branwynn Rynne.
t.Madruga: Chiara Zayden Riqueza was elected as Madruga's senator.
t.Miekarova: Talvikaarne, The Winter Guest, was elected Senator for Miekarova.
t.Necropolis: Eli of the Cenotaph was elected Senator for Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Vesna (Sparrow) Borkovna was elected Senator for Ossium.
t.Skarsind: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected Senator for Skarsind, and RAKK won the title of Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting with 20 votes.
t.Temeschwar: Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar was elected Senator for Temeschwar.
t.Zenith: Cadeus was elected Senator for Zenith.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Branwynn Rynne was appointed by the Senate as Grimnir of Wittal Grove.

384YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.d: With 1184 thrones in the treasury, the Senate funded a fourth Wintermark army (400 thrones), Marcher military resupply (500 thrones) and the Black Canal. It ceded Trajadoz to its Marracossans, opened free trade with the Sarcophan Delves and retrained a historical researcher to produce appraisals. It created the Witness of Conclave and gave the Imperial Seer a stipend. Commissions included Thornsong House, the Temeschwar Department of Architecture, Atalaya Harbour, the Golden Cascade, a fortification in Lustri and several Zenith rebuilding projects. The treaty with Kaliact, the Great Chains of Sarvos and the Academy of Arms expansion failed. Ambassadors to the Iron Confederacy, the Grendel, Axos and Jarm were elected.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Senators were active: the Laroc tournament grounds in Astolat received 50 thrones, Semmerholm proposed the Cerevado Nets and Weirwater secured a 40-throne stipend for the Imperial Seer.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the miasma pillars that the Senate began clearing from Zenith are described as Druj miasma.
n.Grendel: Abel of Zenith Ascendant of Urizen was elected as the Empire's Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highborn Senators proposed an appraisal on encouraging foreign pilgrims of the Way and the retraining of researchers. Reikos's treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact failed.
n.Imperial Orcs: Two orc sept follies were commissioned: the Ossuary Temple in Skarsind for the Illarawm, and an armoury-smithy for the Ethengraw. Research into the orc guards of Empress Ahraz was cancelled.
n.Navarr: Cedric Gallows and Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr were elected ambassadors to the Iron Confederacy and Axos. Navarr Senators secured Thornsong House in Therunin and free trade with the Sarcophan Delves.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn ceded Trajadoz to its Marracossans, creating the Marracossa Sendito. They gained a new ilium bourse seat at Crevado, Atalaya Harbour and a mana ministry in Madruga, and won an appraisal of Kahraman.
n.The League: The League gained an ilium bourse seat in the hills above Tassato and the Temeschwar Department of Architecture. Kleist's Winter Gardens in Holberg ran into complications, and the Great Chains of Sarvos failed.
n.The Marches: The Marches received 500 thrones for military resupply, funds for the Black Canal and 200 thrones for the Golden Cascade. The Imperial Breadbasket aimed at Marcher refugees had no current opportunity to act on.
n.Thule: The new Trading Hall at Wreck is intended to trade food for Thule ilium, helping them feed their people after abolishing slavery.
n.Urizen: Zenith saw extensive investment: miasma clearance, a Lustri fortification, the Golden Cascade, the Crucible of Fate and the Starlight Drift. Urizeni Abel and Ariadne were elected ambassadors to the Grendel and Jarm.
n.Varushka: The Crawling Depths in Ossium was renamed, and Miekarova's Witness of Conclave title was created. Karsk's motion to expand the Academy of Arms failed.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark won funding for a fourth army raising in Sermersuaq, an expansion of the Pride of Ikka's Tears mithril mine and a Trading Hall at Wreck.

t.Astolat: The Laroc tournament grounds are to be built in Astolat, with 50 thrones disbursed to its Senator.
t.Bastion: The pilgrims appraisal may focus on escalating Bastion and the Bay of Catazar territories to the challenge of Timoj. Bastion's Senator also seconded the Black Canal funding.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's Senator proposed retraining a historical researcher and seconded the pilgrims appraisal.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark's Senator proposed and received 400 thrones to raise a fourth Wintermark army, which will raise in Sermersuaq.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia's Senator seconded the Imperial Seer stipend and the Iron Confederacy ambassador election, and called the unsuccessful Throne election.
t.Holberg: Kleist's Winter Gardens, a herb sinecure at the Holberg University Duelling Grounds using Skathe's Winter curse, was announced but has run into complications.
t.Kahraman: An appraisal of how to restore Kahraman's recently destroyed infrastructure, including revised Cinnabar Roads proposals, will be published before Spring.
t.Kallavesa: The new Wintermark army is supported by consecrating the Kallavesa marshes. Kallavesa's Senator also proposed the Trading Hall at Wreck.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov's Senator proposed ambassador elections for the Iron Confederacy and the Sumaah Republic, and seconded the Trading Hall at Wreck.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's Senator seconded the Crawling Depths renaming and proposed the failed Academy of Arms expansion.
t.Madruga: The town of Trajadoz in Madruga was ceded to its Marracossans. The Parador of Salt and Sand, a mana ministry, is being built in Quzar.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren's Senator proposed free trade with the Sarcophan Delves and seconded the Axos ambassador election.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova's Senator proposed the Witness of Conclave title and seconded the Commonwealth ambassador appointment.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: 500 thrones for military resupply were disbursed to Mitwold's Senator, who also seconded the Tassato hills motion.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow's Senator proposed the Zenith miasma clearance and seconded the Lustri fortification.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold's Senator proposed and received 200 thrones to rebuild the Golden Cascade in Zenith, and seconded the Witness of Conclave.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis's Senator proposed the pilgrims of the Way appraisal and seconded the retraining of researchers.
t.Ossium: Ossium's Crawling Depths mine and seat was renamed the Vale of the Sunless Depths, though locals favour simply Sunless Depths. Bones recovered from Ossium will rest in the Ossuary Temple.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's Senator proposed the Ossuary Temple and seconded the Ethengraw armoury.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos's Senator proposed the failed treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact and seconded Thornsong House.
t.Sarvos: The proposed Great Chains of Sarvos fortification to protect Sarvos and the south coast failed.
t.Segura: A new Brass Coast bourse seat will net ilium from the Scorrero river at Crevado in Segura, and Segura's Senator secured Atalaya Harbour.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm's Senator proposed the Cerevado Nets and seconded the Temeschwar Department of Architecture.
t.Sermersuaq: A fourth Wintermark army will begin to raise in Sermersuaq, and a Trading Hall to buy Thule ilium will be built at Wreck in East Floes.
t.Skarsind: The Ossuary Temple will be built in Southpine, Skarsind, and ceded to the Illarawm sept to house bones recovered from Ossium.
t.Tassato: The hills above Tassato will be exploited for ilium, creating a League bourse seat chosen by business owners.
t.Temeschwar: The University Department of Architecture will be built in Hanuri, Temeschwar, creating the Master of Rings title.
t.Therunin: Thornsong House, a hospital college for potion research overseen by the Thornsinger, will be built in Therunin.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's Senator proposed and received 19 thrones and 6 crowns for the Black Canal in the Marches.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz's Senator seconded the failed Kaliact treaty and proposed the Jarm ambassador election.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater's Senator secured a 40-throne seasonal stipend for the Imperial Seer and seconded the Cerevado Nets.
t.Zenith: Zenith's miasma pillars will be cleared at 75 thrones a season until it is cleansed. Projects include the Lustri fortification, Golden Cascade, Crucible of Fate and Starlight Drift.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Skathe's Winter curse on Holmauer Park is to be channelled through Marcher menhirs to grow herbs in Kleist's Winter Gardens, a commission now facing complications.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The Crucible of Fate, a foundry rebuilt where the ushabti were first created, is being constructed in Iteri.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Senate commissioned a fortification in Lustri, requiring Senate funds over the year.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The Starlight Drift of Shimmering Snow, a mana sinecure at Endsmeet, is being reconstructed in Occursion.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Golden Cascade in Proceris is being reconstructed with 200 thrones from the Senate.

384YE Winter Solstice Synod judgements.d: The change of doctrine to accept Freedom/Anarchy as a virtue failed 18 to 1485. The Assembly of Nine ruled that Anarchy remains a false virtue and that future liberations must be inspired by the Seven Virtues. The General Assembly narrowly refused Lenarius Ankarien's call to exterminate the Druj and instead urged soldiers to question orders to slaughter them. Enacted mandates gave every congregation 36 rings from Free Folk visits, removed the final bar to the Free Folk joining most nations, roused the League and Varushka against the Vyig, and welcomed the Great Forest Orcs into Navarr. True liao went towards rebuilding Zenith, and many appointments, inquisitions and vindications followed.

n.Dawn: Dawn's assembly sent Pelleas Montrose to inspire the Dawnish in the Barrens, which opens a chance for Dawnish generals to meet the Dawnish resistance there at the Spring Equinox. It also proposed Owain of House Wolfbourne as chaplain to its generals and called for a more open, glorious voting system.
n.Druj: The Synod narrowly refused a mandate to exterminate the Druj by any means, condemned 'Death to the Druj' as hateful, and urged soldiers to question orders to slaughter them. Urizen and Varushka nonetheless called for the Druj to be scoured from Zenith and destroyed.
n.Grendel: Highguard urged that Grendel traders in Necropolis who seek lasting ties be welcomed, but the merchants of the Broken Shore would not commit as their treaty nears its end. The League called for debate with Grendel visitors, and the Imperial Spymaster was called to inquisition over spy networks in Grendel territories.
n.Highguard: Highguard's mandates will subtly change how the Highborn view the lineaged and orcs, and they give its assembly the Peerless Kinship and Partner of Greatness abilities for a year. Funding liao tutelage for the Free Folk costs every Highborn business a rank of production for the rest of the year. Several assemblies also named imperial tombs in Necropolis as stops on a pilgrims' trail.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc assembly's mandate stops Stonecliff Brakkalo from affecting the nation further. The virtue fund paid 11 Thrones towards mithril for the Ethengraw Armoury so that the Ethengraw sept can join the nation, and the Winter Sun's march to break shackles in the Barrens was upheld with primacy.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher folk hero William Guildenstern was praised for fighting in the Valiant Hurricane Battle, where 12 Marchers faced 50 Jotun and 12 ogres.
n.Navarr: Navarr's mandate welcomes the Great Forest Orcs to make steadings in Miaren and Hercynia, while rival calls to send them on or to throw them a festival failed. Navarr also celebrated rediscovering all the cities of Terunael, urged guides to help the Navarri bandits in Therunin, and elected Teleri Thornweaver as Voice of Barbs.
n.The League: League congregations preaching Ambition gain an extra liao and two extra Synod votes until Winter 385YE, and a mandate rouses the League to end the Vyig. Its assembly also endorsed donations for the chains of Sarvos, called for outreach to the Grendel, and rejected any Highguard mandate to interfere in its virtue.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly urged Vigilance to refute Mathilda Fisher's words in Bregasland, resolved to teach the Way to Mournwold orcs who wish to join the Empire, and named William Guildenstern a Marcher folk hero. Bastard Tom was appointed Keeper of the Orchard.
n.Thule: Varushkans freed from Ossium were urged to support the Thule through a harsh winter after they ended slavery, and Wintermark's call for cultural exchange at the Wreck trade hall was withdrawn. Iron Osric and Lofyn Bloodcloak were vindicated over the Thule treaty, while the Ambassador to Otkodov was given penance.
n.Urizen: Mandates without a greater majority have little effect on Urizen. Its assembly urged resistance to Highguard influence, sent sword scholars to cleanse the Druj legacy from Zenith, and invited persecuted Suranni to settle in Urizen. True liao and 30 Thrones were awarded towards rebuilding Zenith.
n.Varushka: Mandates without a greater majority have little effect on Varushka, so the Free Folk mandate does not open the nation to them. Its own mandate rouses Varushkans to end the Vyig, and its assembly welcomed Iron Confederacy refugees, declared that the Druj must be destroyed, and urged recognising virtue in sapient creatures.
n.Wintermark: The caves beneath Runegrott were consecrated as a tomb for the first runesmith so that work on Runesmith's Law can begin. Wintermark priests in Sermersuaq, backed by the Loyalty assembly, will hunt those who accepted Blood-on-the-Snow's aid, and the Assembly of Nine sent the Silent Bell to investigate the cults there. Beodun Snowlock entered the Chronicle of Heroes.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: a note says Grendel merchants grew more eager to trade along the northern coast of the Bay of Catazar in what may be their last chance before the treaty ends.

384YE Winter Solstice interlude.d: The Imperial Guerdon stood at 350 thrones, shared among units supporting Quiet Step, Gryphon's Pride, Valiant Pegasus and the Beacons of Kallavesa. Opportunities opened to explore the heart of Terunael, assault the Aerie of the Slave Lords, venture into the Twisted Woods, explore the sinkhole depths and map the Sea of Snow. Spring-infused rains brought extra herbs to most of the Empire. Semmerlak flotsam enriched Semmerholm and Weirwater. Tharim's black frost drained Dawn in return for aid against the Barrens. Enchantments settled on the Mournwold and Zenith. Congregations swelled under the Reject False Gods mandate. The Empire entered free trade with the Sumaah, the Commonwealth and Axos, while Nemoria closed to Imperial fleets.

n.Dawn: Dawn suffered Tharim's black frost, which cost every Dawnish mana site and farm until the Autumn Equinox 385YE in return for steel-bound knights aiding any Dawnish army attacking the Barrens. Dawnish units gained bonuses for Dark Ranging, exploring Terunael and entering the Twisted Woods.
n.Druj: The Druj-held Barrens faced Dawnish armies reinforced by Tharim's steel-bound knights for the coming year, and the territory was spared the storms' rejuvenation.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun-held Bregasland and Liathaven were excluded from the storms' herb bounty, and the earlier raid on Skallahn opened new fleet options for Marcher and Wintermark captains.
n.Navarr: With help from the Great Forest Orcs, Navarr in Therunin, Hercynia, Miaren and Brocéliande could improve herb gardens for one fewer wain of weirwood until the Summer Solstice 385YE. Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging attracted extra Dawnish support.
n.The League: League congregations in Temeschwar and Tassato swelled under Rafael Barossa di Tassato's anti-idolatry mandate, and Holberg's farms received herbs from the Sand Fisher orcs.
n.The Marches: A Winter enchantment let the people of the Mournwold speak to and lay ghosts to rest. Marcher fleets gained a new Raid along the Gullet Shore action and could map the Sea of Snow at full strength.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained a congregation boost in Redoubt and an Autumn enchantment easing new starts in Zenith, though Zenith missed the storms' herb bounty. New rituals were added to Urizen lore.
n.Varushka: Varushkan units were especially effective Into the Twisted Woods, with permanent access promised should the Tower of the Manticore be built in Ossium. Karsk's congregations were strengthened, but Varushka shunned the Semmerlak flotsam under its Assembly's mandate.
n.Wintermark: The Beacons of Kallavesa shared in the Guerdon, Hahnmark's congregations grew, and Wintermark fleets could Guard the Fisherfolk of Westerhal and map the Sea of Snow at full strength.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland had been spared the supernatural storms and so received none of the rejuvenating herbs granted elsewhere.
t.Brocéliande: Brocéliande became the focus of an expedition towards Terunael and of Dark Ranging with extra Dawnish rewards. Navarr herb gardens there could be improved more cheaply, though the territory missed the storms' herb bounty.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained additional votes and liao while the Synod stood clearly against idolatry, because a building designed by the Asavean architect stood there.
t.Hercynia: Navarr with herb gardens in Hercynia could improve them for one fewer wain of weirwood thanks to the Great Forest Orcs.
t.Holberg: Farms in Holberg received two random herbs each season from the Sand Fisher orcs' tithe.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Beacons of Kallavesa were among the efforts sharing in the Imperial Guerdon.
t.Karsk: Congregations in Karsk gained additional votes and liao as long as the Synod clearly opposed idolatry.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven had been spared the storms and so did not benefit from the Spring-infused rains' extra herbs.
t.Miaren: Navarr herb gardens in Miaren could be improved for one fewer wain of weirwood until the Summer Solstice 385YE.
t.Mournwold: A potent Winter enchantment let anyone in the Mournwold freely speak to the shades of the dead and more easily placate and lay them to rest.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: building the Tower of the Manticore in Ossium would give Dawn and Varushka permanent access to the Twisted Woods action.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt gained additional votes and liao while the Synod maintained its anti-idolatry stance.
t.Sea of Snow: The Senate funded an attempt to map the Sea of Snow and the western coast, open to fleets with Wintermark and Marcher captains operating at full strength.
t.Semmerholm: Every business in Semmerholm gained extra crowns and rare-metal ingots from strange flotsam washing up from the Semmerlak.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the raid on Skallahn led to new fleet actions for Marcher and Wintermark captains.
t.Tassato: Congregations in Tassato swelled with pride under the anti-idolatry mandate enacted by Rafael Barossa di Tassato, gaining extra votes and liao.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar gained additional votes and liao while the Synod clearly opposed idolatry.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens faced Dawnish attacks backed by Tharim's steel-bound knights and were excluded from the storms' herb bounty.
t.The Semmerlak: Strange flotsam washed up on the Semmerlak's shores, enriching businesses in Semmerholm and Weirwater, though Varushka warned its people away from it.
t.Therunin: Navarr herb gardens in Therunin could be improved for one fewer wain of weirwood with the Great Forest Orcs' help.
t.Weirwater: Every business in Weirwater gained extra crowns and rare-metal ingots from the Semmerlak flotsam.
t.Zenith: An Autumn enchantment helped travellers, traders and settlers in Zenith find their feet and windfalls, though Zenith missed the storms' herb bounty.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Dawnish units supporting Dawnish, Highborn or Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging earned an extra crown and two herbs under Ranae de Rondell's mandate.

384YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: Zenith was wholly reclaimed and its ruined lands awaited restoration. The Jotun left Sermersuaq, leaving fortifications and lingering troubles behind them. Imperial armies in the Barrens held the line rather than seize the Fangs, and tried to win over the territory's inhabitants. Other winds covered Great Forest Orcs seeking homes in Navarr, a Freeborn scheme to steal the Scorrero Nets from Feroz, a runeforge project in Wintermark, ghosts in the Mournwold, new Thule offers, consecrations at the Maze of Zoria and Ratibor's Torch, and Highguard mandates. Shorter notes covered sabotaged Kahraman roads, flooding in Ossium, higher costs to build in marshes, and senatorial election concerns.

n.Dawn: Dawnish enchantresses had until the Summer Solstice to win five Summer eternals as patrons of the Eastern Sky. Dawn had also welcomed the Free Folk, and its glory-seekers were drawn to monster-hunting in Wintermark and Varushka.
n.Druj: The Druj had been driven out of Zenith into Sarangrave and were on the back foot in the Barrens, though they dug in at Ossium's Drownbark Forest and still held captured Navarri vates.
n.Grendel: Grendel Governor Rahab's rule over Feroz was the target of an audacious Freeborn plan to steal the Scorrero Nets. The Grendel port of Oran remained closed to Imperial fleets.
n.Highguard: A surge of Pride in Highguard after the Druj defeats led to three potent mandates that might change how the nation sees itself and the faith. Highguard was also tagged in the Barrens strategy and the Free Folk question.
n.Imperial Orcs: Three proud septs in Skarsind sought reassurance before joining the nation, and the Thule made new offers to the Imperial Orcs. Perhaps half of the Tamazi had already become Imperial citizens.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had left Sermersuaq behind fortifications and a claim on Ikka's Tears, while the Lasambrian Jotun sabotaged Kahraman's mountain roads and raided caravans from Liathaven. They lost an outpost in Bregasland and Jarl Snekmar's warband.
n.Navarr: Some Great Forest Orcs sought new homes in Miaren and Hercynia, a fork in the road that might fundamentally change the nation. Navarri healers calling themselves the vines had to decide who they were.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn weighed Ottilie i Malune i Erigo's scheme to steal the Scorrero Nets from Grendel-held Feroz. Their assembly celebrated the freeing of Thule slaves and voiced concern over Senate elections, while Kahraman caravans faced danger.
n.The League: The Chair of the Wolf was due to be appointed, sparking talk of a contest to name the greatest League city. The consecration of Ratibor's Torch spread an aura of Ambition, and secret chambers beneath the Imperial Mint were being drained.
n.The Marches: Marcher yeomen had to choose where to direct the Breadbasket now that Urizen was mostly whole, amid trouble with the Mournwold orcs. The Greensward's ghosts could be eased, and Sarcombe's growing prosperity offered opportunities.
n.Thule: After the Thule Dragons outlawed slavery and the Senate lifted tariffs, northern trade grew and the Thule made offers to Wintermark and the Imperial Orcs. The Wintermark runesmiths they had enslaved returned home.
n.Urizen: Zenith was again wholly Urizeni, and the Empire set about restoring a territory the Druj had left in ruins, though miasma pillars and the Endless Stalker remained threats.
n.Varushka: The consecration of the Maze of Zoria drew pilgrims and whispers of the sovereign beasts, while lesser beasts stirred and the Varushkan assembly questioned its Senate elections. Flooding in Ossium was worsening.
n.Wintermark: With Sermersuaq freed, Wintermark faced lingering scars, the questions of those who took the Choice, and a Jotun legacy to build on. Returned runesmiths gathered at Runegrott to complete a northern runeforge.

t.Bregasland: The higher cost of building in marshes applied in Bregasland, where a Jotun outpost in the Grey Fens was eliminated during an Autumn conjunction.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: odd fruit gathered on an adventure there was noted as a magical matter, and the higher cost of building in marshes applied there.
t.Feroz: Feroz suffered under Grendel Governor Rahab, and the Brass Coast weighed a daring plan to steal the Scorrero Nets from under his nose.
t.Hahnmark: Many returned master runesmiths gathered at Runegrott in Hahnmark, where only the consecration of a tomb for Isenbrad remained before a runeforge could be built.
t.Hercynia: Some Great Forest Orcs wished to establish new homes in Hercynia, a request with deep implications for Navarr.
t.Holberg: Holberg university's proposed Chair of the Wolf had been established and was due to be appointed at the Solstice. Pumps imported from Holberg were draining the chambers under the Imperial Mint.
t.Kahraman: Jotun sabotage had wrecked roads and bridges in northern Kahraman, so the Cinnabar Roads plans were obsolete. It was proposed that the Senate fund caravan guards to protect the mithril and white granite trade.
t.Karsk: A small group of Varushkans visited the Mir Mozga at Pyotr's Square to investigate the strange behaviour of the Ketsov; the outcome was not common knowledge.
t.Liathaven: The Lasambrian Jotun struck at Kahraman caravans from a base in southern Liathaven, their return there worried the Marches, and the higher cost of building in marshes applied.
t.Madruga: Rerouted Kahraman caravans now passed through Madruga at risk of raiders, a spreading blight troubled the territory, and heroes freed Sumaah pilgrims in Calvos Sound.
t.Miaren: Some Great Forest Orcs wished to establish new homes in Miaren near the weirwood groves.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: people were beginning to speak of the Mournwold as Mitwold's equal in prosperity and importance.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: the Axos were angry about Imperial involvement in the failure of their joint venture with the Grendel into the Mountains of the Moon.
t.Mournwold: A necromantic enchantment offered a chance to ease the Greensward's hauntings, and Sarcombe's booming trade raised prospects for prosperity. There was also worrying trouble with the local orcs.
t.Ossium: Flooding was worsening in southern Ossium, forcing settlers from their homes and possibly threatening the Crawling Depths. The Druj had dug in at Drownbark Forest.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: it was where the Thule had taken enslaved Wintermark runesmiths, and Thule merchants from Otkodov interested some Tamazi.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Senator Sejanus of Redoubt was named among those tagged in the trade winds.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: orc raiders out of Reinos were named as a threat to the rerouted Kahraman caravans.
t.Sarangrave: The Mallum orcs fled from Zenith into Sarangrave, and Navarri vates held at Karliss remained at the mercy of their Druj captors.
t.Sea of Snow: The Imperial project to map the Sea of Snow was completed, and ship captains were returning with news of what they had found.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was free of the Jotun, who left fortifications and lingering scars. Autumn conjunctions there dealt with Jarl Snekmar and rescued Yantl, though Tuuli's Eye was lost.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn was raided by the Empire in Spring, which opened the way for the Sea of Snow mapping, and the Jotun escaped into Skallahn with the stolen relic Tuuli's Eye.
t.Skarsind: The Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende septs in Skarsind awaited reassurance before joining the Imperial Orcs, while many Tamazi settled there and became citizens.
t.Spiral: The Archmage of Night led a conjunction to Kephalos' Delve in Screed, whose outcome was not public knowledge.
t.Tassato: Flooded secret chambers beneath Tassato's Imperial Mint were being pumped out and explored, and Kahraman caravans could no longer take direct routes to the city.
t.Temeschwar: After Laughlan vi Temeschwar consecrated Ratibor's Torch with true liao, an aura of Ambition spread through Ratibor and perhaps the whole League.
t.The Barrens: Imperial armies held the line in the Barrens rather than take the Fangs, sending scouts to win over inhabitants who hated both the Druj and the Empire. The higher cost of building in marshes applied there.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs had lived among the Navarr in Therunin for some years.
t.Volodmartz: A conjunction at Urodli's Fall in Brez led to fighting whose exact outcome was not common knowledge.
t.Zenith: Zenith was again part of Urizen but lay in ruins. An appraisal, Prosperity priests, a potent enchantment and the armies were all turned to its restoration.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: An Autumn attack on a Jotun outpost at Jayne's Top Copse succeeded, and the general of Mandowla's Roar paid a heavy price.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the pumps sent to the Imperial Mint resembled those used at the Great Pits of Ennerlund.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Sabotaged roads made travel through Braydon's Jasse extremely difficult, greatly reducing the effectiveness of Fort Braydon.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Damatian Cliffs forewoman Catalina i Burna i Riqueza was rescued at Talaeiros and returned to work.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Caravans from the Great Mine of Briante now took longer routes, and the Lasambrian Jotun were already striking at those leaving Serra Briante.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Damaged roads forced white granite caravans from the Damatian Cliffs onto dangerous detours through Madruga.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Imperial heroes in Calvos freed Sumaah pilgrims from a malicious creature and drove it off.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The permanently haunted Greensward fell under a necromantic enchantment that offered a chance to ease its worst hauntings.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Sarcombe in Southmoor was flourishing as a trading town, and some spoke of it as a rival to Meade.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Druj dug in around Petka's Path despite Imperial efforts, prompting the Winter Sun to move to Ossium.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: The rivers of Nearweald were rising, partly because of swathes of felled trees, forcing settlers from their homes and possibly threatening the Crawling Depths.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: An attempt to rescue Navarri vates from Karliss failed, and they remained Druj captives.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Jotun escaped from Avointaivas into Skallahn with Tuuli's Eye, but Yantl the Storm Runner was intercepted at Broken Rock Plain and their pursuer presumably dealt with.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Jarl Snekmar and his warriors were dealt with at Kilpailuala Bay and no longer threatened Sermersuaq.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: Mentioned in passing: some Tamazi were keen to visit the Illarawm sept in Southpine to share their appreciation of bone.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Archmage of Night's conjunction to Kephalos' Delve had an outcome that was not public knowledge.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Imperial forces advanced towards the Fangs but chose not to take them, holding the line while scouts carried a message of hope to the inhabitants.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Sorin unleashed his hungry wolves to aid the Imperial armies, and some remained to guard the lands of House Aurelius.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Senate had reiterated its intent to concede the Heart of Peytaht and its weirwood grove to the Great Forest sept once the Barrens was conquered.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: Fighting took place at Urodli's Fall, but the outcome was not common knowledge.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The miasma pillar at the Pallasian Steps still stood, anchoring the Druj miasma in Iteri.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Mallum orcs were forced out of Lustri, but its miasma pillars still stood and the Endless Stalker remained a threat to its people.
r.Zenith/Occursion: A miasma pillar at the Field of Celestial Mist was destroyed, but efforts to stop weapons reaching the battle and to disrupt the Druj at the Tower of the Fall failed.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The miasma pillar at the Plantation of Tall Ferns still stood, anchoring the Druj miasma in Proceris.

384YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: The Jotun were expelled from Sermersuaq with Thule help. Lasambrian Jotun pressed into Kahraman, Mathilda Fisher claimed western Bregasland, and war returned to Liathaven. Four armies guarded Kallavesa through an uneventful season. In the east the Druj fought their way out of Zenith to the Sarangrave, with half their armies paying the full price, and Zenith returned to Imperial hands. The push along the Steel Causeway in the Barrens met stiff resistance and achieved no decisive result. The Winter Sun crushed Druj saboteurs in the Drownbark Forest. Liberty Pact forces razed Rachensgrab, and champions used Rhianos's cauldron to reach Terunael. Five battle opportunities and many conjunctions were offered for the coming summit.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies faced a heavier penalty to conquest in the Barrens, could not take cautious or yielding orders, and gained better resupply at home after Barrens campaigning. One Barrens battle opportunity aimed to capture a Dawnish collaborator.
n.Druj: The Druj were driven out of Zenith into the Sarangrave, with half their fleeing armies paying the full price. They all but held the Imperial advance in the Barrens, while their saboteurs in the Drownbark Forest were routed.
n.Highguard: Highborn armies could no longer issue the Crusading Storm order but might generate mandates for their assembly wherever they campaigned. They also gained advantages when attacking Zenith from Morrow or defending Morrow.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Tusks stood guard in Kallavesa. The Imperial Orc general Rykana led the Winter Sun to smash Druj saboteurs in the Drownbark Forest in support of Varushka.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were driven from Sermersuaq and showed no sign of attacking Kallavesa. They pressed south instead: Lasambrians targeted Kahraman, they honoured Mathilda Fisher's claim to Bregasland, and they fought again in Liathaven.
n.Navarr: Navarr's ancestral heartland of Brocéliande was the target of a daring expedition, backed by Rhianos's cauldron, that reached the walls of Terunael. Navarr was offered conjunctions there to recover the Tairiscint na Foraoise and rescue injured Marchers.
n.The Brass Coast: Lasambrian Jotun sought to seize the hills of Kahraman and its mithril and white granite. A conjunction aimed to stop them ambushing wagon trains in Serra Briante.
n.The Marches: Mathilda Fisher claimed western Bregasland, and the Jotun stood once more at the threshold of the Mourn. Marchers helped man the Wintermark beacons, and Mournwold conjunctions sought to rescue Wise Maggie and stop Little Robin reaching Liathaven.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were driven from Sermersuaq by Imperial strength allied with Thule cunning.
n.Urizen: Zenith was returned to Imperial hands after the Druj fled. Urizen was warned that the Citadel Guard would begin to deteriorate again after the Summer Solstice.
n.Varushka: The Winter Sun came to Varushka's aid, blocking Druj attempts to wreck roads and bridges in the Drownbark Forest. Varushkan armies remained hampered when campaigning alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark forces.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq was freed of the Jotun, and Kallavesa was guarded all season without incident while Winterfolk stood ready at the beacons. Wintermark armies kept their honour-bound edge against the Jotun.

t.Bregasland: Mathilda Fisher claimed the western marshes as her fiefdom with Jotun backing, though there was resistance. A battle opportunity offered the chance to rouse Old Marjoram and arrest a Marcher traitor.
t.Brocéliande: Champions from almost every nation used Rhianos's cauldron to delve into the vallorn, pressing right to the heart of the forest and through the walls of Terunael.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian Jotun sought to claim the hills for their mithril and white granite, following earlier Jotun attempts that had all been thrown back.
t.Kallavesa: The Drakes, the Fist of the Mountains, the Summer Storm and the Tusks held defensive positions in the marshes all season, but the Jotun never came.
t.Liathaven: War came again to Liathaven as the Jotun exploited the weakness of the vallorn. A battle opportunity offered the chance to destroy keystones and use the Spring regio.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army could take the Billet order in Mitwold.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Highborn or Urizen armies defending Morrow against an attack from Zenith gained an advantage.
t.Mournwold: With the Jotun once again at the threshold of the Mourn, conjunctions in Southmoor aimed to rescue Wise Maggie and keep Little Robin from reaching Liathaven.
t.Ossium: The Winter Sun blocked Druj insurgents trying to destroy roads and bridges in the Drownbark Forest. Its orcs made short work of the Mallum saboteurs after Imperial heroes failed to win a decisive victory.
t.Sarangrave: The Druj armies fleeing Zenith, slowed by curses and chains of glass, were forced to seek sanctuary here.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate in Semmerholm could not be reduced below a set military strength.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun were driven out by Imperial strength and Thule cunning. Conjunctions were offered in Stark and Tanikipari.
t.Skallahn: A battle opportunity was offered here to save an Imperial spy network from destruction and stop a fane being built.
t.The Barrens: Imperial armies fought savagely to extend the Steel Causeway, but the Druj all but held their advance. Two battle opportunities and several conjunctions were offered here.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army could take the Billet order in Upwold.
t.Zenith: The Druj fought their way out under curses and pursuit, and Zenith was once again in Imperial hands. Conjunctions were offered in Iteri, Lustri and Occursion.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: A conjunction to the Orchard of Tom Wiscall, overseen by the General of the Strong Reeds, aimed to deliver resources to the Scraggy Bole.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: A conjunction to the Dry Marsh, overseen by the Blackroot Broker, aimed to rescue Tall George, an apprentice of Mott.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: A conjunction to the Silent Copse, overseen by Avery Farkas, aimed to rescue a number of injured Marchers.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: The cauldron-backed expedition penetrated the walls of the city of Terunael, and a conjunction to Kay's Lament sought to recover the Tairiscint na Foraoise.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: A conjunction to Isabella's Track aimed to kill Lasambrian Jotun before they could ambush wagon trains.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: A conjunction to the Cold Path of Kaisa aimed to kill Lasambrians before they slaughtered a group of Hylje.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Two conjunctions were offered here: one to rescue Wise Maggie at Tollerton Green, and one at Friar Tommy's Grave to stop Little Robin reaching Liathaven.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Druj insurgents tried to destroy vulnerable roads and bridges here until the Winter Sun intervened and crushed the Mallum saboteurs.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: A conjunction to Vahne's Field aimed to force the Jotun to retreat.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: A conjunction to Siward's Folly aimed to defeat Jarl Roneth and return the sword to Barien.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: A conjunction to the Broken Glade, overseen by the Apothecary of Orieb, aimed to kill the Sleepless Nightmare.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Two conjunctions targeted Druj here: killing the Burnt Fist coven at Berena's Tree and Garsnag Mudchurner at his holt.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: A conjunction to Soulflayer's Refuge, overseen by the Champion of Vigilance, aimed to kill Varag Soulflayer.
r.Zenith/Iteri: A conjunction to the Spire of the Everlasting Dusk, overseen by the High Exorcist, aimed to lay tortured souls to rest.
r.Zenith/Lustri: A conjunction to the Spire of Twisting Shadow, overseen by the Senator of Zenith, aimed to destroy miasma pillars.
r.Zenith/Occursion: A largely peaceful conjunction to the Ring of Solace ruins aimed to lift spirits and investigate.

All too well.d: None of the three follies that would reassure the septs (Ethengraw Armoury-Smithies, Illarawm Ossuary, Yerende Gardens) had been started. In Gildenheim, Stonecliff Brakkalo denounced the Empire's neglect and urged Imperial Orc armies to stay in Skarsind and raise the money themselves. The Imperial Orc assembly could silence her or endorse her with a Synod mandate; otherwise dissent would grow. The Illarawm offered to teach shaman a meditation that quiets intrusive ancestors. The Yerende offered orcsroot to the House of the Broken Shield in exchange for alpine cultivation lore. Inspired by Thanmir Hrafnar's statement, the Ethengraw approached Wintermark, offering to move to Hahnmark if forges were built, possibly alongside the planned runeforge.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are remembered as the cruel former masters of the Ossium septs, whose oppression shaped their traditions and fears.
n.Imperial Orcs: The nation faced growing dissent from Stonecliff Brakkalo, who urged its armies to withdraw to Skarsind, and its assembly could answer her by Synod mandate. It also had open offers from the Illarawm to help its shaman quiet troubled ancestors.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr stridings carried Great Forest Orcs through Skarsind, took a few Yerende away with them, and escorted Ethengraw emissaries through Hercynia.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Brakkalo complained of white granite going to Marcher canals, and the Mournwold was cited as a precedent for questions about orcs joining a nation.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs' earlier refusal to fight while the Empire was allied with slave-owning Otkodov inspired Brakkalo, and the Thule Dragons have since decreed an end to the practice.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Brakkalo complained that Ossium was freed and handed to the Varushkans, and a Varushkan trader told the Illarawm of Bloodcrow Udoo's efforts.
n.Wintermark: Moved by Thanmir Hrafnar's welcome to heroes of any origin, the Ethengraw asked the Winterfolk to build them forges, possibly adding 45 wains of mithril to the planned runeforge. In return they would come to work there and one day seek to join the nation.

t.Hahnmark: Ethengraw emissaries led by Amadi Thunderstone came to Kalpaheim, and thousands of Ethengraw would move to Hahnmark if Wintermark built them forges.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw emissaries travelled through Hercynia with a Navarr striding on their way to Hahnmark.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: earlier questions about orcs joining a nation in the Mournwold, settled by a Senate appraisal, were cited as a precedent.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is the homeland the three septs left behind, freed from the Druj and now held by Varushka.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's alliance with slave-owning Otkodov prompted the Imperial Orc generals' earlier withdrawal, which inspired Brakkalo.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the new Hall of the Unbroken in Sermersuaq is named among the Empire's efforts to help new citizens.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was home to the three unintegrated Ossium septs and to Brakkalo's preaching, which risked pulling the nation's armies home and stirring dissent if left unanswered.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs, a Barrens sept, appear to be distant kin of the Yerende.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs suggested the Yerende might be happier in Therunin, though the sept as a whole showed no wish to move again.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Brakkalo preached in Gildenheim, where the Ethengraw are mostly settled and where their proposed Armoury-Smithies would be built.
r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The Yerende in Solvihill struggled with alpine soil and offered 8 doses of orcsroot to the House of the Broken Shield in exchange for lore on growing Cerulean Mazzarine.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: The Illarawm in Southpine, site of their proposed Ossuary, offered to teach visiting Imperial Orc shaman a meditation for quieting angry or fearful ancestors.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs suggested the Yerende might one day settle beneath the boughs of the Heart of Peytaht.

At the dog and eel show.d: After three Marcher national assembly statements, from Edward Greenfriar, Bryce Tanner and Sister Meredith, the yeofolk, backed by the alders of Meade and Sarcombe, asked the civil service to hold a tally of votes among those with farms. Feed the Wizards would send seed, livestock and cuttings to Zenith for a year in return for mana, letting Urizen support the Citadel Guard without the Golden Cascade and afford a navy at Elos. Beat the Bounds would add 1,000 force to Imperial campaigns in Mitwold, Mournwold and Upwold, and to the Strong Reeds in Bregasland. Tend the Hearth would give farms extra rings and cheaper upgrades. Separately, orc leaders led by Hap the Soft met at Golden Hoof amid heated argument, and about fifty orcs walked out.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr traveller described the venomous Druj creatures now infesting Zenith's marshes and lakes, which Bregas listeners thought might be farmed like eels.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Marcher farmers asked whether cargo bound for Zenith would travel quicker through Highguard or Therunin.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were out in force in Bregasland and massing in Liathaven, which drove the Beat the Bounds option, while the gathering of their former thralls near the border made Marchers uneasy.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr traveller Lindir told the Dog & Eel's taproom about Zenith and was teased for not knowing the difference between poisonous and venomous.
n.The Marches: Marcher farm-holders were to decide in a tally of the votes how their farms would spend the next year, whether aiding Zenith, supporting the beaters against the Jotun, or improving their own farms, while beaters watched an unexplained orc gathering in the Mournwold.
n.Urizen: If the yeofolk chose Feed the Wizards, Marcher farms would help rebuild Zenith's agriculture for a year, letting Urizen sustain the Citadel Guard without rebuilding the Golden Cascade and become prosperous enough to support a navy at Elos.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Druj creatures in Zenith were likened to the octopuses of the Bay of Catazar.
t.Bregasland: Held by the Jotun, Bregasland was the source of Marcher worry, and under Beat the Bounds the Strong Reeds would gain 1,000 strength while fighting there; under Tend the Hearth even Bregas farms would gain the extra rings.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun were massing in force in Liathaven, recalling to Marchers the build-up before the Mourn fell, and news of it coincided with the thralls' gathering.
t.Mitwold: Under the Beat the Bounds option, any campaign in Mitwold would see 1,000 additional force added to the Imperial side for a year.
t.Mournwold: Beat the Bounds would add 1,000 force to Imperial campaigns in Mournwold, and the territory's orcs, the former Jotun thralls, gathered there in a tense and secretive meeting.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Marcher farmers asked whether the roads through Therunin or Highguard were the quicker route to Zenith.
t.Upwold: Under the Beat the Bounds option, any campaign in Upwold would see 1,000 additional force added to the Imperial side for a year.
t.Zenith: Newly recovered by Urizen and facing serious problems, including Druj creatures in its marshes and lakes, Zenith stood to receive a year of Marcher seed, livestock and fruit cuttings if the yeofolk chose Feed the Wizards.

r.Mournwold/Green March: About five hundred former Jotun thralls camped around Golden Hoof farm in Green March at Hap the Soft's call, turned Marchers away, and argued for days until about fifty walked out before the rest dispersed in silence.

Bad blood.d: Jenny Arbor's Marcher assembly statement named six Urizeni casters, including Archmage of Spring Ibiss of Netherwatch, Imperial Inquisitor Galene and the once-declared sorcerer Aquillian, plus two facilitators and a person of interest. Rafael Barossa di Tassato's Concord was ruled equivalent to an endorsement, so the magistrates and militia dropped their case, though priests and magicians may still act. Alisoun Bathwater urged threshers to investigate those involved through the Assemblies and the Conclave. The proposed title, appointed by Declaration of Candidacy, could raise one Declaration of Sorcery per session. Depending on its remit, Marcher threshers offer four Thresher's Cudgels a season, Necropolis's Umbral Shroud the Lantern Ring, and Miaren's Lost Lore Steading a yearly Thornpath Sash. The offer lapses at the end of the Spring Equinox 385YE.

n.Highguard: Highborn magisters, who believe magical study should be paired with the study of virtue, want the proposed title to watch closely over anyone dealing with eternals. A dwindling group from Necropolis has offered the Lantern Ring as regalia on that condition.
n.Navarr: Navarr vates, mindful of Terunael's fall and the creation of the vallorn, want the title to keep watch over all powerful magicians before hubris leads them astray. Lost Lore Steading has offered a yearly Thornpath Sash if the title investigates Conclave-appointed title holders.
n.Urizen: All six named casters of Thunderous Deluge are prominent Urizeni, including the Archmage of Spring, the Imperial Inquisitor and Aquillian of Urizen, and some suspect Urizen's mountain-dwelling economic interests behind the flooding. They are safe from the magistrates but face possible investigation by threshers, the Assemblies and the Conclave.

t.Miaren: The vates of Lost Lore Steading in Miaren have offered a Thornpath Sash each year, a focus for several investigative rituals, if the new title is charged with ensuring Conclave-appointed title holders are not corrupted by their power.
t.Necropolis: The Umbral Shroud, a once-powerful order of Necropolis magisters from Empress Giselle's reign, has offered the Lantern Ring, which can reveal whether someone has recently visited a chamber between worlds, if the title watches those dealing with eternals.

Burning.d: Imperial heroes, joined by Commonwealth, Sumaah and Axou ships, used charts seized at Chalonsio to reach Rachensgrab. Abel, Bursar of Conclave, was recognised by the General Assembly as Admiral of the Great Fleet. The armada overwhelmed the docks, where crews of many foreign ships fought alone and were sunk, captured or fled. Champions slew the herald Pharam Vex and burned his temple, while Ajakstu of the Many Masks leapt to their death from the Sacrificial Tower. A blockade sank or seized most fleeing ships. Guided by freed slaves through hidden tunnels, the attackers stormed the aerie, killing the slave lords and their leader Feetla. The vaults were looted, and Jarm and Asavea must now adapt.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: several Grendel cogs were among the foreign vessels at Rachensgrab's docks, which were overwhelmed, sunk or forced to flee.
n.Urizen: Abel of Zenith Ascendant, Bursar of Conclave, was recognised as Admiral of the Great Fleet, pledged mana to captains joining the raid, and gained the captured fleets and Autumn ritual texts to distribute.

t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith appears only in the name of Zenith Ascendant, the group to which the Admiral Abel belongs; nothing happened in the territory itself.

Cede Trajadoz.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by Segura, the motion passed at no cost to the Empire. Trajadoz now belongs to the Marracossan exiles, who may run the town as they please, including constructing buildings such as the temple they had previously requested, provided they have the materials. The motion created the title of Marracossa Sendito, a Brass Coast national position appointed annually at the Spring Equinox by Tally of the Votes of the fleet owners. The Sendito represents the Empire to the Marracossans and vice versa, and holds a ministry allowing the purchase of magic items made by the émigré artisans, some of them unknown in the Empire.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gained a new national Bourse title, the Marracossa Sendito, chosen each Spring Equinox by its fleet owners, which acts as the link to the Marracossan exiles and gives access to their artisans' unusual magic items.

t.Madruga: The town of Trajadoz in Madruga was handed over to the Marracossan exiles, who are now free to govern it and build there, including the temple they had asked for.

Chime the sound.d: The warlock Lirk, speaking for Tathenon, offered a ritual text unknown to Imperial lore in exchange for the original herbal almanac the Imperial Orcs took from the Druj. The trade would be completed over several summits, starting with a winged messenger to Rak. Freynir offered the ancient mask Strágríma, whose wearers hear whispering voices, if Thule warlocks could study the Shepherd of the Great Herd for a season, halving its output. With the Thule short of food, a Senate motion could create a charitable caravan, needing at least 50 Thrones to help and 200 to help greatly. Two Freeborn mandates would send priests to Otkodov, either urging freed slaves south or urging virtue on the Thule; either would provoke a diplomatic incident.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the almanac the Thule seek was taken from the Druj, and the freed humans sent south were former Druj slaves.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs received two Thule offers: a ritual text in exchange for their original Druj herbal almanac, and the mask Strágríma in exchange for hosting warlocks studying the Shepherd of the Great Herd. Both the Preceptor and Shepherd positions were vacant at the time.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn Synod statement noted that the Thule sought Imperial help because they are in danger from the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn could encourage the Thule's abolition of slavery by sending a charitable food caravan north. Their priests could also travel to Otkodov under either of two prepared mandates, both of which would risk a serious diplomatic incident.
n.Thule: Facing a food shortfall after freeing their slaves, the Thule sought Imperial knowledge through offers by Tathenon and Freynir. They might receive charitable food, or Freeborn preachers they would strongly resent.
n.Varushka: Thule merchants appeared in Varushka after the tariffs were lifted. Its national assembly urged preparation for travellers, and some of the freed human slaves arrived in northern Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Thule merchants were trading in Wintermark, which had already received two Thule offers. Freed human slaves arrived in eastern Seremersuaq, and Thule diplomats told Wintermarkers of Otkodov's food shortage.

t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn Synod statement contrasted aiding the Thule with travelling to Kahraman to kill wounded Lasambrians.
t.Karsk: Some of the roughly eight hundred freed human slaves of the Druj were returned into northern Karsk, where priests and others worked to house them and find them work.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: a Synod statement declared that the House of Guerra in Madruga will always welcome refugees.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the Thule ambassador Rak dwells at the Embassy to Otkodov in Miekarova, where messages about both offers must be sent.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the slaves the Thule liberated from the Druj in Ossium and sent into Varushka were all human.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov faced short-term starvation after its slaves were freed. It could receive a charitable Imperial food caravan, or Freeborn priests preaching to its people at the risk of a major diplomatic incident.
t.Skarsind: The Thule offers were aimed at Skarsind's orcs: the senator for Skarsind or the Preceptor of its College of Warcasting would need to answer Lirk's proposed trade of a ritual for the Druj almanac.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi was noted as the only part of Otkodov the Empire knows much about.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mentioned in passing: Mieriada is where Rak's Embassy to Otkodov stands, the destination for winged messengers accepting the Thule offers.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: The Thule hoped to reproduce the Imperial Orcs' fenceless herding techniques in Nithoggir's open lands if Freynir's warlocks were allowed to study them.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Urdur was named alongside Nithoggir as land where the Thule hoped to apply the herding methods learned from the Shepherd of the Great Herd.
r.Verthandi/Askja: Mentioned in passing: the region itself is not discussed; the name appears only through the Thule diplomat Askja of Volham, who hinted at Otkodov's food shortage.

Construct Atalaya Harbour.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Kahraman, the motion built the harbour described in the wind of fortune The power behind our moves, at a cost of 10 wains of weirwood, 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns in labour, with upkeep of 5 thrones a season. Gancio di Catazar supplied the money and materials after the Winter Solstice. Once complete, any Freeborn fleet based in Madruga can be upgraded each season for one less weirwood. The Grendel cannot legitimately claim it breaches the existing treaty, though they recognise the threat. The docks could later be expanded cheaply into a full shipyard. The discount lasts only while the new arrivals stay in Madruga, and many would likely go home if Feroz is reclaimed.

n.Grendel: The Grendel cannot legitimately claim the new docks breach the existing treaty, but they are aware of the threat the harbour poses as a possible future shipyard.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn fleets based in Madruga gain cheaper upgrades from the harbour, which relies on shipwrights among the new arrivals, many of whom would return home once the Brass Coast reclaims Feroz.

t.Feroz: Feroz, held by the Grendel, is home to many of the new arrivals now working in Madruga, and its reclamation by the Brass Coast would draw them home and end the harbour's upgrade discount.
t.Madruga: Atalaya Harbour is rebuilt in Madruga, letting fleets based there upgrade for one less weirwood each season, with the option of later expanding it into a full shipyard.

Construct Crucible of Fate.d: Acting on the Write your own ending wind of fortune, Sagua i'Ezmara chose Zenith over Kahraman, arguing that while Kahraman's roads were broken, Zenith's spirits were. The project costs 30 wains of white granite, 20 wains of mithril, 10 rings of ilium and 15 thrones, and takes six months. Funding was organised by Zenith Ascendant from Urizeni donations, and Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged provided the full materials after Winter Solstice 384YE. Once complete, the Urizen National Assembly would be able to endorse a mandate encouraging Zenith to embrace a new destiny as the Crucible of Fate, and 140 ingots would be split equally between the businesses of the League.

n.The Brass Coast: Sagua i'Ezmara, as Master of the Koboldi, directed this season's construction effort to Zenith rather than to Kahraman's broken roads.
n.Urizen: The Urizeni gain a rebuilt workshop of spiritual and physical significance, and their National Assembly would be able to endorse a mandate shaping Zenith's identity once it is complete; Zenith Ascendant gathered donations from Urizen's people to fund it.

t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the announcement noted that Kahraman's roads were broken, but the project was directed to Zenith instead.
t.Zenith: Zenith is to regain the Crucible of Fate, described as a focal point for defining the territory's identity, with a mandate offering it a new destiny as the Crucible of Fate once the six-month construction is complete.

r.Zenith/Iteri: The Crucible of Fate foundry, the workshop where the ushabti were first created, is to be rebuilt in Iteri, with all its materials provided after Winter Solstice 384YE.

Construct Department of Architecture.d: The motion followed the Back in the same place Wind of Fortune. Construction cost 60 wains of white granite, 30 wains of weirwood, 180 crowns and six months. Asael, Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Karo Di Yedinso supplied the money and materials after the Winter Solstice 384YE and Spring Equinox 385YE, and the building was completed. The Master of Rings holds one civilian build commission a season and access to a white granite, mithril and weirwood ministry, and is charged with generating wealth for Temeschwar's merchant-princes and the League. The title was first available by League Tally of the Votes at Summer Solstice 385YE. The Constitutional Court noted that the motion's removal clause was invalid for a Tally-appointed title and sought a clarifying administrative motion.

n.The League: The League gained a new national title, the Master of Rings, appointed by League Tally of the Votes and charged with enriching the merchant-princes and the nation, although the proposed removal by League, General or Assembly of Nine was constitutionally unworkable.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's university gained a Department of Architecture, built largely with granite, weirwood and money supplied by Temeschwar citizens, and the motion was proposed by Temeschwar's own senator.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Hanuri was the site of the new Department of Architecture, which was completed after funding arrived following the Winter Solstice 384YE and Spring Equinox 385YE.

Construct Ethengraw Armoury.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by the senator for Redoubt, the motion commissioned a smithy and armoury in Gildermark, to be given to the Ethengraw. The motion text cited 60 wains of mithril and 120 crowns, while the cost recorded on the page was 60 wains of mithril and 15 thrones, with six months to complete. After the Winter Solstice the full 60 wains and the thrones were provided by many donors, led by Bloodcrow Rasp (19 wains and the 15 thrones) and Tulva (10 wains). Once complete, the Ethengraw will join the Imperial Orcs. They will form the core of any new Imperial Orc army, offer chances to muster one, and allow a unique army quality reflecting their fighting arts.

n.Imperial Orcs: Once the armoury is finished, the Ethengraw will join the Imperial Orcs and form the core of a possible new Imperial Orc army, with the option of a unique quality drawn from their fighting arts.
n.Varushka: The folly is to be raised in Gildermark in Varushkan-held Ossium and ceded to the Ethengraw sept who live there, so it will draw that sept into the Imperial Orcs.

t.Ossium: A smithy and armoury folly is to be built in Gildermark for the Ossium-based Ethengraw sept, funded with 60 wains of mithril and due to take six months to complete.

Construct Kleist's Winter Gardens.d: The commission followed the In the garden of defiance wind of fortune. Marcher menhirs would turn the lingering Winter curse on Holmauer Park to growing herbs. Kleist von Ennerlund, Vintners and Victuallers of Holberg, offered to fund it themselves, and after the Winter Solstice 384YE Lula Kleist von Ennerlund provided 15 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of white granite and 3 thrones 6 crowns. The work took three months. It was finished once work on Holberg's Melodious Cascade was complete. The new Imperial title, Tender of Kleist's Winter Gardens, is appointed annually by Imperial Bourse auction, which brings coin into the Senate budget. It was to be auctioned for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.The League: A League family, Kleist von Ennerlund, paid for the gardens out of its own resources, framing it as an act of loyalty to the Empire and to their beloved city of Holberg.

t.Holberg: Holberg gains a new herb-producing sinecure at its University Duelling Grounds, turning the scars of the Hag Queen's attack into a resource under the defiant cry "Holberg Endures!"

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Skathe's Winter curse on Holmauer Park is put to use, with Marcher menhirs channelling its magic to grow herbs in the new Winter Gardens.

Construct Laroc Tournament Grounds.d: The motion passed at 50 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Astolat. The work required 40 wains of weirwood, 10 thrones and three months. Ren Tanner and Guy Grimbold-Antenucci each supplied weirwood after the Winter Solstice 384YE and again after the Spring Equinox 385YE, and Ren Tanner also provided the 10 thrones. Once complete, the grounds would act as a great work giving every business in Astolat a share of 743 rings. In the season of completion, the Castellan of Spiral Castle could raise up to a dozen Dawnish-owned military units to rank 2. For a year afterwards, Dawnish units could be upgraded for one wain of mithril less. The Senator for Astolat would choose the grounds' colours and decorations.

n.Dawn: Dawn stood to gain a grand tourney ground in Astolat, with up to a dozen Dawnish-owned military units upgraded to rank 2 through the Castellan of Spiral Castle, and cheaper mithril upgrades for Dawnish units for a year.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the page names only the Castellan of Spiral Castle and says nothing about Grendel or its people.

t.Astolat: The Laroc tournament grounds were to be built in Astolat, giving every business in the territory a share of 743 rings once complete, with the Senator for Astolat choosing their colours and decorations.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the only link is the title of the Castellan of Spiral Castle, who would choose which Dawnish units were upgraded; nothing happens in the territory of Spiral itself.

Construct Ossuary Temple.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by the senator for Skarsind, the motion followed the All too well Wind of Fortune. The temple needed 60 wains of white granite, 15 thrones and six months to complete. After the Winter Solstice the materials were largely supplied by Bloodcrow Rasp, who gave 14 thrones 6 crowns and 31 wains of granite. Many Irontide orcs and others gave smaller amounts of granite, and Fintan Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov each gave a crown. Once the temple is complete, the Illarawm will join the Imperial Orcs. They will share knowledge of their ancestors and help the nation hear its own ancestors' voices better.

n.Imperial Orcs: Once the temple is complete the Illarawm sept will join the Imperial Orcs and help the nation better hear the voices of its ancestors; Bloodcrow, Irontide and Stormsteel orcs supplied most of the granite and coin.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the bones the temple will house were recovered from Ossium, a territory Varushka held at the time.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is where the Illarawm sept recovered the bones the temple will house.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind is to gain the Ossuary Temple, a folly ceded to the Illarawm sept, and its senator seconded the motion.

r.Skarsind/Southpine: Southpine is the site of the new Ossuary Temple, which will take six months to build and will house the Illarawm sept's recovered ancestral bones.

Construct Parador of Salt and Sand.d: The commission cost 15 wains of mithril, 5 wains each of white granite and weirwood, and 50 crowns, and would take three months to build. Small contributions came in after the Winter Solstice, and Bakar i Riqueza supplied the full materials and most of the money after the Spring Equinox 385YE. Once complete, it creates the Brass Coast title of Hakima of Salt and Sand, appointed by Tally of the Votes. The Freeborn are expected to elect only a hakima, and there would be consequences otherwise. The Parador could later be upgraded into a College of Magic. If upgraded, and while the title-holder is a hakima in good standing, the Empire's college upkeep would fall by 20 thrones a season.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gain a new national title, the Hakima of Salt and Sand, chosen by Tally of the Votes. They are firmly expected to elect only a hakima to it and to support a community of hakima who could aid magical research.

t.Madruga: The Parador is built in Quzar, strengthening that city's central importance in Madruga. It could later be expanded there into a full College of Magic.

Construct Thornsong House.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Reikos, the motion took up an opportunity from the Make a deal Wind of Fortune. Construction required 120 wains of weirwood and 30 thrones, took nine months, and carries an upkeep of 10 thrones a season. Many individuals, mostly Navarr, contributed weirwood and coin between Winter 384YE and Summer 386YE. Once complete, the Navarr title of Thornsinger was to be appointed for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 386YE, by Tally of the Votes of Navarr herb garden owners. The Thornsinger controls a ministry, may address the Senate to announce a research focus, and oversees the development of new ways for apothecaries to use herbs.

n.Navarr: Navarr gained the new title of Thornsinger, chosen annually by the nation's herb garden owners, to lead potion research and control a ministry. Navarr citizens provided much of the weirwood and coin needed to finish the hospital college.

t.Therunin: Therunin's senator proposed the motion, and Thornsong House was built in the territory to honour its heritage of healers and apothecaries. It now stands as the Empire's centre for potion-lore.

Construct Trading Hall at Wreck.d: Proposed by Kallavesa and seconded by Karov, the motion created the Trading Hall at Wreck as set out in the Write the lines wind of fortune. Its holder, the Mediator of Wreck, is appointed by the Tally of the Votes of Wintermark. The motion's stated aim was to help the Thule feed their people and follow a prosperous path after abolishing slavery. Construction required 8 wains of weirwood, 16 crowns in labour and three months. Funding was gathered from several donors after the Winter Solstice 384YE and Spring Equinox 385YE. Once complete, the Mediator can send shipments of food to the Thule in the Silver Peaks in exchange for rings of ilium.

n.Thule: The Thule in the Silver Peaks will be able to receive Imperial food shipments in exchange for rings of ilium, a trade intended to help them feed their people after abolishing slavery.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new ministry whose holder, the Mediator of Wreck, is appointed by the Tally of the Votes of Wintermark, giving the nation control of food-for-ilium trade with the Thule.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq becomes the site of a trading hall at Wreck linking the Imperial and Thule-held parts of the territory through trade in food and ilium.

r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Trading Hall at Wreck is built in the East Floes, from where the Mediator of Wreck will dispatch food shipments to the Thule.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule in the Silver Peaks are the intended recipients of food from Wreck, paying for it in rings of ilium.

Don't blame me.d: The tomb was consecrated by Laughlan vi Temeschwar after a Synod judgement. Its torches now barely go out, and pilgrims leave inspired. The League assembly may enact mandates to spread Ambition, to destroy the Vyig, who are regrouping in Varushka and are tied to the bite trade, or to burn out Skathe's servants haunting Metri. Metri has disrupted the Northern Trade Network and raised the Fortress of Salt's upkeep. Proposed projects include modernised mines in Locul, a timbermill in the Vardstein Vale and a mana exchange for trading with the Thule. Any Ambition mandate would tinge League opportunities with ruthlessness for a year. Varushka may also respond to Ratibor's legacy.

n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc thief-takers could be hired, and Imperial Orc military units could join the Break the Vyig adventure if the League enacts the mandate to destroy the Vyig.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's Hercynia is linked to Temeschwar by the Northern Trade Network, which the Metri troubles and a proposed Thule exchange would disrupt.
n.The League: The League gained its only memorial to a specific exemplar. Its assembly can spread Ambition, destroy the Vyig, cleanse Metri or back great works, but any Ambition mandate would make League opportunities ruthless and unsentimental for at least a year.
n.Thule: Thule traders pass through Metri unharmed by propitiating the Mirror of Spite. A proposed Temeschwar market would draw most of their mana crystal trade into the League.
n.Varushka: The Vyig have rebuilt in old Varushkan bolt holes. Varushkan priests may submit alternative mandates on the Vyig, Varushkan units could join their destruction, and a strongly supported statement of principle about Ratibor could spread Ambition through the nation.
n.Wintermark: The Vyig have placed a bounty on the Winterfolk cardinal Veikko Bondforger, mistaking him for Ratibor reborn. Wintermark's Hahnmark is part of the disrupted Northern Trade Network.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is linked to Temeschwar by the Northern Trade Network, whose ministries are disrupted by the Metri haunting. Its traders would lose the top levels of their Thule trade if the proposed Temeschwar exchange is built.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia is a western link in the Northern Trade Network, now disrupted by the dangers in Metri. It would lose Thule trade to a proposed Temeschwar mana exchange.
t.Holberg: Holberg is praised for turning the eternals' enmity to its own ends. If the larger Ambition mandate passes, a chance would open to build an art structure there, and Holberg's mechanisms would inspire the proposed Temeschwar mines.
t.Karov: Karov is the eastern link of the Northern Trade Network, which the Metri troubles disrupt and a Thule exchange in Temeschwar would undercut.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the robber-boyar Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch, possibly funded by the Vyig, had his attempt to raise a bandit army in Karsk stymied.
t.Otkodov: The Thule of Otkodov trade mana crystals through the Northern Trade Network. A proposed Temeschwar-Otkodov Mana Exchange would channel most of that trade to Temeschwar.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's Blood Red Quays Art Gallery would switch from supporting Pride to Ambition if the larger mandate passes. The city was where the earlier purge of the Vyig began.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Trade Network runs east from Temeschwar to Karov via Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Tassato's Blood Red River Museum would switch to supporting Ambition under the larger mandate, which would also offer a chance to secure materials to finish repairing it.
t.Temeschwar: Ratibor's Gate now burns with near-eternal torches and draws pilgrims. Temeschwar faces Vyig violence and Skathe's creatures in Metri, and is offered great works in its mines and forests, a Thule mana exchange, and higher taxes if these succeed.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: the wilderness outside Temeschwar's walls is compared to that of Volodmartz.

r.Temeschwar/Locul: The Descent Guild of Ore Extraction proposes the Mines of Temeschwar great work to modernise Locul's mines. It would provide rings to mines and ingots to businesses, and raise Temeschwar's taxation by 5 thrones a season.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: The creatures haunting Metri slaughtered a caravan, disrupting the Northern Trade Network and raising the Fortress of Salt's upkeep. A League mandate or the Order of the Rod and Shield could clear the haunting.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Vardstein Timber proposes building the Vardstein Timbermill and Sorting Yard on the edge of the wild Vale. It would supply forest materials, create the Vardstein Vandal title and clear land for farming.
r.Temeschwar/Vargat: Mentioned in passing: a road built for the proposed Vardstein timbermill would pass through Vargat, making its fertile soil easier to reach.
