Drums beat in my head.d: The Scorrero Nets in northern Oranseri sieve ilium washed down the river, and since Feroz fell to the Grendel their yield has gone directly to Governor Rahab. Ottilie, who fled Feroz along with scores of netriggers now living in Cerevado, pointed out that the same ilium must pass Cerevado first. The Senate is offered a motion costing 200 thrones, with 5 thrones upkeep and three months' work, to create a Bourse seat at Cerevado producing 4 ilium each season. If built, it would render the Scorrero Nets useless. The parador masters promise to donate 60 thrones if the seat is allocated to the Brass Coast as a National Seat, and they urge other Freeborn to donate too.

n.Grendel: Governor Rahab stands to lose all the ilium from the Scorrero Nets, the jewel of his rule in Feroz, if the Empire builds the Cerevado Nets upstream.
n.The Brass Coast: Displaced Freeborn netriggers could regain their livelihood, and the Brass Coast could gain a National ilium seat. The parador masters of Cerevado offer 60 thrones if the Senate allocates the seat to the nation.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Scorrero's ilium would otherwise be lost in the deep waters of the Bay of Catazar.
t.Feroz: The Scorrero Nets, which Rahab seized and turned into his palace, would be left useless if the proposed Cerevado Nets were built upstream.
t.Segura: The town of Cerevado, which shelters many netriggers who fled Feroz, could become home to a new ilium Bourse seat on its dangerous rapids.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Scorrero Nets in northernmost Oranseri, now worked by Grendel slaves for Governor Rahab, would be starved of ilium by the proposed upstream nets.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Lucksprings is the proposed site of the Cerevado Nets, a Senate motion to build a seat producing 4 ilium each season from the Scorrero rapids.

Enchanted.d: A Winter blight centred on the House of Aldea di Tutamen was turning Madruga's Great Grasses to desert, peopled by water-hungry husks. Hakima asked for Spring rain magic, such as Regrow the Land's Heart, and for a single order to investigate. Chaos fruit from Brocéliande worked like unpredictable potions and could, for a limited time, be cultivated in forests using Rampant Growth. Other items included the Gift of Kaela, fanes and the Arcane Architect, Tharim's offer to ward the Hall of Worlds, a proposed scholars' base at the Brilliant Star, and a Key and Lock conjunction. The page also covered new sorcerers, magical fortifications and shrouds, and additions to Urizen lore.

n.Druj: Their territory, the Barrens, remained under a Penumbral Veil. The Gift of Kaela was discussed as a way for Imperial citizens to escape Druj capture, and perhaps to free the tormented souls the Druj create.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Aldea di Tutamen trace their roots to the exodus from Highguard, and the Highborn Ephrael, Jaylus and Keritoth were listed among the sorcerers active at Anvil.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: their territory Liathaven was named among the vallorn-afflicted lands where cultivating chaos fruit might be dangerous.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia and Therunin were named among the vallorn-afflicted territories where cautious horticulturalists warned against cultivating chaos fruit.
n.The Brass Coast: A Winter blight was turning the Great Grasses of Madruga into desert. The Freeborn hakima appealed to the Conclave for Spring-infused rain and an order to investigate, following Raphael i Zamora i Riqueza's warning to the National Assembly.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: their territory Sarvos remained under a Penumbral Veil that hindered divination.
n.The Marches: A great wall of thicket and burr was raised in Alderly in the Mournwold, and a Marcher coven reported an unsettling hour of compulsive singing after casting Wisdom of the Balanced Blade.
n.Urizen: The Hall of the Newborn Sun accepted the Synod's judgement on Lucidianism and added the Book of the Restless Spirit rituals to Urizen lore. Zenith gained a thicket wall in Lustri and remained shrouded, and students sought a base in Redoubt's Brilliant Star.
n.Varushka: Ossium was fortified with the Dripping Echoes of the Fen in Drownbark Forest and a thicket wall in Echofell, and remained under a veil. The Varushkan magicians Aleksandr Novosad and Claudia Varkulova Remys championed the fane and Tharim declarations.
n.Wintermark: Fog-shrouded fortifications lay over Kallavesa's three marshes. Lumi of Wintermark would receive a partial refund if the Brilliant Star's output were cut, and Aethelric the Grounded was listed among Anvil's sorcerers.

t.Brocéliande: Explorers returned from the vallorn-haunted woods carrying chaos fruit, which could only be used for cultivation if freshly plucked from vallorn and planted before the end of the Spring Equinox 385YE.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory with an active vallorn where cultivating chaos fruit might be dangerous.
t.Kallavesa: Mists and heavy fog were raised as magical fortifications over Kallavesa Marsh, Rundhal Marsh and West Marsh.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory with an active vallorn where cultivating chaos fruit might be dangerous.
t.Madruga: A slowly growing desert, caused by Winter magic and haunted by water-hungry husks, was spreading from the House of Aldea di Tutamen and threatened the Great Grasses and possibly all of Madruga. Only water, ideally Spring-infused, slowed it.
t.Mournwold: A great wall of thicket and burr summoned from the Spring realm was raised in Alderly.
t.Ossium: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in Drownbark Forest and a thicket wall was raised in Echofell, while a Penumbral Veil still hung over the territory.
t.Redoubt: The Spire of the Seventh Mist sought a Senate motion to establish a base in the Brilliant Star mithril mine. This would cost four wains of mithril a season but would improve the Doyen of the Spires' ability to codify Day rituals.
t.Sarvos: A Penumbral Veil still hung over Sarvos, which divinations would first need to overcome.
t.The Barrens: A Penumbral Veil still hung over the Barrens, which only Piercing Light of Revelation could remove early.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory with an active vallorn where cultivating chaos fruit might be dangerous.
t.Zenith: A thicket wall was raised in Lustri, and a Penumbral Veil still hung over the territory.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Mists coiled and fog lay heavy over Kallavesa Marsh as a magical fortification.
r.Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh: Rundhal Marsh was wrapped in fortifying mists and heavy fog by Imperial magicians.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: West Marsh was blanketed in fortifying mists and fog during the Autumn Equinox.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: A great wall of thicket and burr was summoned from the Spring realm to fortify Alderly.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose here to support the Winter Sun had the Druj tried to reclaim the land.
r.Ossium/Echofell: A great wall of thicket and burr was raised in Echofell as a magical fortification.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Mentioned in passing: Tomari is not named on the page, which links it only through the proposal for scholars to base themselves in Redoubt's Brilliant Star mithril mine.
r.Zenith/Lustri: A great wall of thicket and burr was summoned from the Spring realm to fortify Lustri.

Establish Cerevado Nets.d: Proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by Weirwater, the motion enacted the opportunity described in the Drums beat in my head wind of fortune. The project cost 200 thrones, took three months to complete and carries an upkeep of 5 thrones a season. Funding came from several citizens after the Winter Solstice, chiefly Gancio di Catazar (127 thrones) and Delara of the House of the Wanderer (just over 70 thrones), with smaller sums from Bakar i Riqueza, Maria i Espiri i Guerra and others. Once complete, the Cerevado Nets became a new Brass Coast Bourse seat producing 4 rings of ilium each season.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gains a new Bourse seat, the Cerevado Nets, adding a source of ilium to the nation's holdings, with funds raised partly by Freeborn citizens such as Bakar i Riqueza and Maria i Espiri i Guerra.

t.Segura: Nets and traps were to be set at Cerevado to harvest ilium from the Scorrero river, creating a Bourse seat in Segura producing 4 rings of ilium each season.

Exploit Tassatan Hills.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Mitwold, the motion took advantage of the opportunity in the Light upon the Water wind of fortune, presented by Gemma Stewart of Tassato on behalf of the city's mining guilds. With the guilds' help the ilium seat cost only 75 Thrones and three months to complete. A single motion both created the seat and made it a League national position. Small donations came from Fintan Nighthaven, Otmar van Holberg, Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos and Nikolai Dravi, while Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato provided the bulk, 74 thrones 4 crowns, after Spring Equinox 385YE. The Tassatan Hills were then complete.

n.The League: The League gained a new national bourse position producing ilium, its holder appointed by a Tally of the Votes of League business owners.

t.Tassato: The hills above Tassato were opened up for ilium extraction with the help of the city's mining guilds, with Tassato's senator proposing the motion and Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato funding most of the cost.

Fire on fire.d: After the Empire took Lustri, seven Druj armies were trapped in Proceris and Occursion. Imperial heroes disrupted their Night enchantment, but four armies were still shrouded. As the Druj fled toward Sarangrave, the Eastern Sky and Golden Axe held Lustri, and perhaps four thousand orcs died. The Hounds of Glory and Citadel Guard then stormed Proceris and Occursion for around three hundred Imperial casualties. Under a Highborn Assembly mandate, the Seventh Wave and Granite Pillar freed most tormented souls and destroyed many Druj warbands, so Zenith was neither terrorised nor under threat. Miasma pillars remain, Proceris is a poisoned swamp, and the territory lies devastated.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies were central to the victory: the Eastern Sky held Lustri against the fleeing orcs, and the Hounds of Glory led the heedless charge that broke the Druj defences in Proceris and Occursion.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Zenith entirely, and perhaps four thousand orcs died fleeing through Lustri. The unshrouded Arrow Viper, Hidden Snake and Poison Blade suffered worst, and the Druj failed to leave the territory terrorised.
n.Highguard: Driven by the Highborn Assembly's mandate, the Seventh Wave and Granite Pillar freed most of the tormented souls, many forged from captured Highborn soldiers, and hunted down Druj guerrilla camps. Some displaced Urizen have begun new lives in Highguard.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is cited as an earlier example of Druj spite in destroying what they cannot hold.
n.Urizen: Zenith was freed, with the Citadel Guard helping to trap and assault the Druj. However, the Urizen return to shattered spires and ruined farms, and many exiles have settled elsewhere and may be reluctant to come home.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe held fast in Lustri alongside the Eastern Sky and inflicted a heavy toll on the fleeing Druj armies.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Empire has previously seen the Druj destroy what they could not control.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: some displaced Zenith Urizen have begun establishing new lives in Morrow.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: cited as a recent example of Druj guerrillas left behind to trouble defenders after the armies were driven out.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: some displaced Zenith Urizen have begun establishing new lives in Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: cited, alongside Holberg, as a place that suffered Druj spite when they lost control.
t.Sarangrave: The surviving Druj armies fled north into Sarangrave, where Citadel Guard magic stopped them venturing further. Ghulai allies from Sarangrave were scattered at the Glade of Night Enshrouding.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky's general, Dame Aurum De Castellan, styles herself the star of Semmerholm.
t.Zenith: Zenith was freed and secured, with most tormented souls laid to rest and remaining Druj bands scattered. It is left devastated, with miasma pillars still to be removed and rebuilding under discussion by the Senate and Synod.

r.Zenith/Lustri: The hostile, magically roused forests of Lustri became a killing ground for the fleeing Druj, whose bodies now rot among the ancient trees. Granite Pillar scouts later rooted out guerrilla camps in its far reaches.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Imperial heroes disrupted the Druj Night ritual at the Glade of Night Enshrouding in Occursion. Its mountains were then retaken, and Druj hiding in its caves were hunted down.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris fell after an assault on the Druj night fortress that caused most Imperial casualties. It remains a poisoned swamp full of venomous bog octopuses, its great farms are gone, and its lingering Night magic enhances Dripping Echoes of the Fen regardless of who casts it.

Folklore.d: The General Assembly could pass one of three competing mandates. Work and Worship would boost production in the nations that had welcomed them. Study and Spirituality would bring 36 rings to every congregation. Inspiration and Understanding would swell sinecures and sacred sites. Passing any of them would end the Pride bonus from Rafael Barossa di Tassato's denunciation of the Asavean Architect's idols. Highguard's assembly could fund the training of about a hundred Free Folk priests at the cost of business production. The Free Folk planned to return to Anvil for the Day of the Dead and demanded the return of their miraculous effigy, threatening legal action. Recognising a Divine Family member as paragon or exemplar, or a permissive mandate, would clear their path to citizenship.

n.Dawn: Dawn, where the Free Folk are based and had been welcomed by the Earl of Fools's statement, would see a one-rank bonus to every farm in Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
n.Highguard: The Highborn could enact a mandate costing every Highguard business a rank of production for the year to train around a hundred Free Folk priests in Highborn doctrine. The Inspiration mandate would also enrich congregations in Bastion and Necropolis.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: listed among the nations where the Free Folk had so far spent little time.
n.The League: Congregations in Tassato and Temeschwar would lose the liao and votes they gained from Rafael Barossa di Tassato's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed. The Free Folk had so far spent little time in the League.
n.The Marches: Already visited by the Free Folk and explicitly welcomed through Tom Keeper's statement, the Marches would see a one-rank bonus to every farm in Mitwold, Mournwold and Upwold under the Work and Worship mandate.
n.Urizen: The Study and Spirituality and Divine Family mandates would only reach Urizen with a greater majority, and failing that the Free Folk might face future problems there. Redoubt's congregations would lose their anti-idolatry bonus if any pilgrimage mandate passed.
n.Varushka: Varushka had welcomed the Free Folk through Radomír Oleksandrovych Dvorak's statement and could gain extra metal and materials with a greater majority. Karsk would lose its anti-idolatry bonus regardless of majority, and without a greater majority on the Divine Family mandate the Free Folk might face future problems there.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark, which welcomed the Free Folk through Rikke's statement, would see bonuses to herb gardens in Kallavesa, mines in Hahnmark and farms in Sermersuaq under the Work and Worship mandate. Hahnmark's congregations would lose their anti-idolatry bonus if any pilgrimage mandate passed.

t.Astolat: Every farm in Astolat would gain a one-rank production bonus from the Winter Solstice until the Spring Equinox if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
t.Bastion: Every congregation in Bastion would gain an extra dose of liao and two Synod votes as the Free Folk visited its basilicas, if the Inspiration and Understanding mandate passed.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's mines would gain a one-rank bonus under Work and Worship, but its congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed.
t.Kallavesa: Every herb garden in Kallavesa would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
t.Karov: With a greater majority on the Work and Worship mandate, every mine in Karov would produce an extra ingot and every forest an extra measure of material.
t.Karsk: Karsk's congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed, even without a greater majority.
t.Miekarova: With a greater majority on the Work and Worship mandate, every mine in Miekarova would produce an extra ingot and every forest an extra measure of material.
t.Mitwold: Every farm in Mitwold would gain a one-rank production bonus as the Free Folk helped clear fields, if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
t.Mournwold: Every farm in Mournwold would gain a one-rank production bonus as the Free Folk helped clear fields, if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
t.Necropolis: Every congregation in Necropolis would gain an extra dose of liao and two Synod votes as the Free Folk visited the tombs of the dead thrones, if the Inspiration and Understanding mandate passed.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed, even without a greater majority.
t.Semmerholm: Every farm in Semmerholm would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
t.Sermersuaq: Every farm in Sermersuaq would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
t.Tassato: Tassato's congregations would lose the liao and votes they had enjoyed since Rafael Barossa di Tassato's mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's congregations would lose the liao and votes from Rafael's anti-idolatry mandate if any pilgrimage mandate passed.
t.Upwold: Every farm in Upwold would gain a one-rank production bonus as the Free Folk helped plant crops, if the Work and Worship mandate passed.
t.Volodmartz: With a greater majority on the Work and Worship mandate, every mine in Volodmartz would produce an extra ingot and every forest an extra measure of material.
t.Weirwater: Every farm in Weirwater would gain a one-rank production bonus if the Work and Worship mandate passed.

Fortify Lustri.d: Proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by Weirwater, the motion called for 80 wains of white granite, 20 thrones and a year's work, with upkeep of 10 thrones a season. Progress depended on contributions from individual citizens between Winter 384YE and Summer 386YE. Cadeus gave substantial sums and 23 wains of granite. Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged supplied the final 57 wains of granite and 12 thrones. Once complete, Lustri was protected by The Stork's Gaze. The people of the Mountains of the Moon offered to help, but the Senate did not ask them to take part.

n.Urizen: The Urizen territory of Zenith gained a major defensive work in Lustri, though its construction depended on donations from citizens across the Empire.

t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: the people of the Mountains of the Moon offered to help build the fortification, but the Senate did not ask them to participate.
t.Zenith: Zenith now has The Stork's Gaze, a 3000-strength fortification in Lustri, costing 10 thrones a season in upkeep.

r.Zenith/Lustri: Lustri is now guarded by The Stork's Gaze, a fortification of 3000 strength built from 80 wains of white granite.

Full of sacred sound.d: Highborn armies had fought beside the Urizeni since 381YE, and the liberation of Zenith, together with the ending of slavery among the Axou, Sarcophans, Faraden and Thule and the destruction of Rachensgrab's slavers, rekindled the nation's fire. Highborn generals could no longer issue crusading storm. Instead, any Highborn army on campaign would create a mandate opportunity for the Assembly each season. Three mandates were proposed. Eli of Walter's Tomb urged Highguard to support its sibling nations. Mordecai of the Basalt Throne Chapter urged the nation to strengthen congregations and build places of worship at home. Dinah of the Passine Chapter, backing Lady Josephine's mandate, urged Highguard to put aside prejudice against orcs and the lineaged.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: temples are being raised in Dawn, and the Highborn Assembly has taken a keen interest in Dawnish Assembly affairs.
n.Druj: The Druj had been driven out of Zenith and Ossium, were falling back in the Barrens and were vulnerable in the Sarangrave. Many Highborn now called for their total annihilation.
n.Highguard: Highborn armies could no longer submit crusading storm but would automatically create mandate opportunities while on campaign. The Assembly was offered three compatible mandates: aiding other nations, strengthening the faith at home, and embracing orcs and the lineaged.
n.Imperial Orcs: Dinah argued that Highguard's focus on the human soul may have delayed the orcs' manumission. Lady Josephine's mandate, if enacted, would lead the Highborn to embrace orcs within the Empire.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers were sometimes redeployed to shore up the Western front as the Jotun pressed.
n.Navarr: Highguard had helped the Navarr turn back the vallorn in Brocéliande, so Navarr could not be named for further aid under Eli's proposed Peerless Kinship. The Highborn Assembly had also been considering Navarr Assembly judgements.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among those the Empire convinced to abandon slavery.
n.Urizen: With Highborn help the Urizeni had their home of Zenith back, though it had been devastated. Because of that help, Urizen could not be named for further aid under Eli's proposed Peerless Kinship.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: temples are being raised in Varushka, and the Druj had been driven out of Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Dinah cited the hylje of Wintermark as creatures the Highborn have misjudged.

t.Bastion: Mordecai of Bastion's Basalt Throne Chapter complained that few places of worship were being built there. Her mandate would boost congregations and support new temples and cathedrals in Highguard.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Highguard had helped the Navarr turn back the vallorn there.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Highborn blood was spilled against the Druj there during the long campaign.
t.Necropolis: Mordecai noted that very few temples or basilicas were being raised there. Her mandate would support building places of worship in Highguard's lands.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had been defeated and driven out of Ossium.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Druj once took and devastated Reikos, the same evil Highborn armies kept returning to fight.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were described as vulnerable in the Sarangrave.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Highborn blood was spilled there and the Druj were falling back after victories aided by Highborn generals.
t.Zenith: The comprehensive defeat of the Druj in Zenith, returning the land to the Urizeni though devastated, was the victory that sparked Highguard's surge of Pride.

Gorgeous.d: Sarcophan Alders-Baart merchants returned to sell cursed curios, and Axou apothecaries of Evander and Associates came to trade outside the Forge. Two exiled Faraden nobles planned a curse duel in the Dawnish Glory Square, and four Grendel questioners invited by Clarice Novarion came to debate with the Synod. The late Urizen seer Flavia of Crystal Hall left an undisclosed prize for whoever solves her puzzles. Three Suranni siblings from Shavronne came to sell metal, and Krampus's attendance was uncertain after its Wintermark hall was destroyed. The six weirwood seats, the wayleaves, the rogue declaration and a dose of true liao were auctioned, and several national titles were put to the vote.

n.Dawn: The Faraden curse duel was to be held in the Glory Square of the Dawnish camp, and Dawnish citizens commanding military units were to choose the first Reeve of Boar's Market; the Suranni traders might also seek out Dawnish yeofolk, with whom they had traded well before.
n.Grendel: A small group of bickering Grendel questioners from the Broken Shore visited the Empire as guests of the Synod while peace held, touring Imperial monuments and seeking philosophical debate with Imperial priests in the Senate.
n.Highguard: The visiting Grendel priests toured the Necropolis and the City of Bastion, taking in its tombs and basilicas, including the cenotaph of Emperor Barabbas and the Basilica of Seven Doors.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs who command military units were to choose the new Four Seasons' Boneweaver and the Preceptor of the expanded College of Warcasting, with votes weighted by how often their units had supported an army in the past year.
n.Jotun: Krampus's known connection to the Jotun, and its lack of interest in a new Wintermark hall, raised fears it had relocated to Jotun lands, perhaps Skallahn; the defeat of the Lasambrian Jotun was also noted as having settled matters in Segura.
n.Navarr: Navarr herb garden owners were to choose who controls the Thimble and the Broker of the Invisible Cord, Navarr were paid to carry Flavia's puzzles across the Empire, and questions about the Navarr were thought likely to affect interest in some weirwood seats.
n.The Brass Coast: Bramar in Feroz no longer gave Suranni traders access under Grendel occupation, while Iron Confederacy caravans tested trade links in settling Segura; Flavia had lived and died at the Lyceum in Madruga.
n.The League: League business owners were to appoint the first Chair of the Wolf and a short-term Northbound Trademaster, and a mix-up wrongly cast the Axou traders as an entourage for the now-legal League magician Evander Slak.
n.Urizen: The late seer Flavia of Crystal Hall left most of her collection to her surviving spire to help those returning to Zenith, and one undisclosed item to whoever solves her puzzles, overseen by her executor Advocatus.
n.Wintermark: With the Krampushal destroyed in the collapse of Pakaanan's Pass and the spirit silent for a year, it was unclear whether Krampus would visit the Wintermark camp, and what its absence might mean for the Winterfolk.

t.Bastion: The Grendel questioners visited the City of Bastion, viewing its tombs, monuments and basilicas, including the cenotaph of Emperor Barabbas and the Basilica of Seven Doors.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: referenced only in a brief aside about the obstacles discouraging Suranni trade with the Empire.
t.Casinea: Anvil in Casinea hosted the summit's visitors, with the Grendel questioners arriving in Casinea and renting the top floor of the Sun and Sand Inn in Outer Anvil.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Grendel occupation of Bramar meant the Freeborn town no longer offered Suranni land traders access to the Empire.
t.Madruga: Flavia of Crystal Hall had spent a decade in her apartments at the Lyceum in Madruga and was found peacefully dead in its Quiet Annexe after the Autumn Equinox.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel questioners travelled via the Necropolis on their route to Anvil.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest at Reikos was one of the six weirwood seats put up for auction.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: most Suranni merchants trade through the embassy in Sarvos, and the three siblings set out north from there to Anvil.
t.Segura: With Segura settling after the defeat of the Lasambrian Jotun, a couple of Iron Confederacy caravans explored possible trade links there, though sanctions made such trade unappealing to most Suranni.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the collapse of Pakaanan's Pass sealed the passage between Skarsind and Sermersuaq.
t.Shavronne: The Larbin siblings, rival merchants of Shavronne, joined forces to bring metals mined from its hills to sell directly at Anvil.
t.Skallahn: There was growing worry that Krampus had relocated to Jotun lands, with Skallahn suggested as a possible new home.
t.Skarsind: The collapse of Pakaanan's Pass in Skarsind a year earlier had destroyed both the Clattering Gulley and the Krampushal, leaving Krampus without its hall.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the Weirwater Vales weirwood seat was among those auctioned.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Flavia's collection was to be sold to help members of her spire returning to Zenith.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: Bramar, once a route for Suranni land trade, was under Grendel occupation and no longer gave access to the Empire.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: lies on the Necropolis route the Grendel questioners took on their way to Anvil.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Iron Confederacy caravans explored possible trade links in Anduzjasse as Segura settled after the Lasambrian Jotun's defeat.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: Iron Confederacy caravans explored possible trade links in Anozeseri, though sanctions limited Suranni enthusiasm.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The western end of the pass, collapsed by Eisa Winterborn and her allies a year earlier, remained sealed, its avalanches having swept away the Clattering Gulley and Krampus's hall.

I knew you were trouble.d: Prospero's lieutenant Maestro Fisetojin would meet the Archmage of Autumn with two invited Varushkans. Sorin's court would parley with the Archmage of Winter, questioned the boons requested, and offered to open the Gauntlet of Fangs to Throne candidates if the Conclave declared concord. Kimus would meet only the Archmage of Day and offered three gifts. Eleonaris would bring her Seat of Judgement for the Summer Archmage and declared friendship restored. The Whisper Gallery refused a parley, sought new agents, and cut ties with Luciano Vivaci Rezia di Tassato. Llofir, its Tamarbode garden ravaged, would forgive the Empire only after being granted amity and visiting famine on every Imperial farm.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Prospero's herald arrived at the Castle of Thorns in Astolat, and Sorin's heralds were at first mistaken for Dawnish knights.
n.Highguard: Brother Luke of Highguard, Archmage of Summer, was invited to ascend Eleonaris's Seat of Judgement and have his empery tested, while Llofir's grievance stems from the destruction of its garden in Highguard-held Reikos.
n.The Marches: Should the Conclave grant Llofir amity, Marcher farms would suffer with the rest of the Empire, though the Keeper of the Breadbasket might mitigate some of the effects in Upwold and Mitwold.
n.Urizen: The civil service warned that if Llofir took its retribution, Urizen would face especially severe starvation because it relies heavily on food imported from other nations.
n.Varushka: Prospero specifically invited Loom-Master Borys and Boyar Vasiliy Strascovich of Varushka, or their representatives, to accompany the Archmage of Autumn to a discreet parley on a sensitive matter.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Prospero's genial herald appeared at the Castle of Thorns in Astolat to deliver his response to the Archmage of Autumn.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris's herald spoke of the enduring good relationship between the Fields of Glory and the Catazarri Empire.
t.Mitwold: If Llofir's threatened blight came to pass, the Keeper of the Breadbasket might be able to soften some of its effects in Mitwold, though that would do little for the wider Empire.
t.Reikos: Llofir's garden lay in Tamarbode in Reikos; Imperial armies ravaged it a year earlier, and that attack is the root of the eternal's refusal to parley and its demand for retribution.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm is not named on the page; the nearest link is Eleonaris's reference to the statue guarding the Golden Causeway as a symbol of friendship with the Empire.
t.Upwold: If Llofir's threatened blight came to pass, the Keeper of the Breadbasket might be able to mitigate some of the famine's effects in Upwold.

r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode held the garden Llofir asked only to be left alone; after the Conclave declared it an enemy, Imperial armies destroyed everything living there, which Llofir now means to avenge.

In each line lies another line.d: In Greenwall, Eisa Winterborn and the Autumn herald Blade Quencher were advancing to destroy the Imperial spy network. Holding a rotten palisade at Jarlsward for an hour would save it, and killing the herald would stop a planned fane at the Well of Whispers. At Broker's Wynd, Igya Olgafsdottir was raising a fortress with keystones from Cathan Canae; destroying them would delay it and let the Moonsilver Prince loose forest creatures. A Spring regio there could also be used for rituals, or given to Surut. In Ottermire, the Empire could stop a Jotun causeway towards Mitwold by rousing the marshwalker Old Marjoram, and could seize the traitor Bushel Sykes.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: local folklore recalls that the first Marchers came to the Bregas marshes from Dawn, and the Knight-Protector of Spring, Jasper Hunter scion De Beaumont, is named as responsible for the Kay's Lament conjunction.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces under Eisa Winterborn, Igya Olgafsdottir and their Fisher allies were pressing their gains in Skallahn, Liathaven and Bregasland, and each was open to an Imperial strike that could cost them their fane, their fortress or their causeway.
n.Navarr: Liathaven, now wholly under Jotun control, was the scene of a planned Jotun fortress. Surut's heralds offered the Navarr egregore to burn Liaven's Glen in return for the Spring regio, and an artefact found by fallen Navarri vates could make Thunderous Tread of the Trees easier to cast.
n.The Brass Coast: A Jotun fortress in Liaven's Glen would threaten Kahraman, either as a springboard for invasion or as a base for raiders striking at the important mines and quarries of northern Kahraman.
n.The Marches: Mathilda Fisher and her Jotun allies were building a military causeway through Bregasland towards Oddmire in Mitwold, aided by the traitor Bushel Sykes. A Liathaven fortress might also threaten the Mournwold, but the Empire could rouse Old Marjoram or bring Sykes to justice to stop the rot.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the page does not refer to Varushka or its people directly; it is linked only through its holding of Ossium.
n.Wintermark: A Jotun fane at the Well of Whispers would sit right on the border of Sermersuaq. The destruction of the Greenwall spy network would also strip the advantages held by armies crossing from Sermersuaq or Kallavesa.

t.Bregasland: Jotun and Fisher forces were widening the Otterway into a military causeway towards Mitwold. Imperial heroes could reach Sot's 'Ole to rouse Old Marjoram against it and capture the turncoat Bushel Sykes at the Oathstone.
t.Brocéliande: A conjunction to Kay's Lament in the vallorn offered the chance to recover the Tairiscint na Foraoise, a potent boon for Thunderous Tread of the Trees found by Gwendolyn Sixthstep, though it was guarded by vallornspawn and at least one massive monstrosity.
t.Kahraman: A completed Jotun fortress in neighbouring Liathaven could serve as a springboard for invading Kahraman, or let raiders threaten the mines and quarries of its north.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: armies crossing into Skallahn from Kallavesa would lose their advantages if the spy network fell, and a Kallavesi ritual from Empress Teleri's reign is said to have quietened the Bregas marshwalkers.
t.Liathaven: Igya Olgafsdottir was laying keystone-anchored foundations for a fortress at Broker's Wynd. The Empire could destroy the keystones, use or surrender the Spring regio there, curse the territory with Thunderous Tread, or kill Igya herself.
t.Mitwold: The Jotun causeway from Bregasland would let their armies pour into Oddmire and invade Mitwold more swiftly unless the Empire destroyed it.
t.Mournwold: A Jotun fortress in Liaven's Glen, on Liathaven's eastern glades bordering the Mourn, could act as a springboard for a potential attack into the Mournwold.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named on the page and has no stated role in these events.
t.Sermersuaq: A powerful Autumn fane at the Well of Whispers would sit right on Sermersuaq's border. Losing the Greenwall spy network would also remove the advantages of armies crossing from Sermersuaq into Skallahn.
t.Skallahn: Eisa Winterborn and Blade Quencher were advancing on Greenwall to destroy the Imperial spy network. Holding them for an hour would preserve the network and its benefits, and killing the herald would prevent a fane at the Well of Whispers.
t.Tromsa: If the Greenwall network fell, the Jarl of Kierheim would use the intelligence to destroy the Empire's planned spy network in Tromsa before it was completed. Igya Olgafsdottir is named as daughter of the Jarl of Tromsa.

r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Sot's 'Ole in Ottermire was the conjunction target. Rough music there could rouse Old Marjoram to wreck the causeway, and the traitor Bushel Sykes could be taken at the Oathstone.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Broker's Wynd held Igya's three keystone stockades and the strong Spring regio of the Circle of Unending Growth. Surut offered to burn the whole region to ash if granted dominion over the regio.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Once the Otterway causeway was complete, Oddmire would be under threat from the Jotun, who could pour into the region and lay claim to Odd's End.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Mentioned in passing: the fortress in Tanikipari that still bears Igya Olgafsdottir's name is noted as lost to the Jotun.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Greenwall was the scene of the battle at Jarlsward, where heroes could hold an old palisade to save the spy network near the Well of Whispers and stop Blade Quencher from taking up residence there.

In the lonely hour.d: Dawnish, Varushkan, League and Highguard armies reinforced the Causeway, aided by the Whelpmaster's white wolves and the Bound King's black knights. The Druj fought alongside servants of Arhallogen and a new army bearing crimson brambles. They fought cautiously, relying on their Spring curse. The Empire still holds Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest and is about a fifth of the way to taking Bitter Strand, where the Druj fell back towards the damaged mithril mine at the Fangs. Following the Synod's call, and with the agreement of Dawn's troubadours, emissaries urged the subject orcs to resist the Druj. This slowed conquest and imposed penalties on most armies.

n.Dawn: The Gryphon's Pride led the assault on Bitter Strand under Garravaine De Rondell, who issued his final orders, and the Golden Sun joined them. Dawn's troubadours backed the Synod's call to free the Barrens' subject peoples, which cost Dawnish armies a three-tenths penalty to conquest.
n.Druj: The Druj failed to close the Steel Causeway and were forced to cede parts of the Bitter Strand shoreline. They fielded the Black Wind, a mysterious new crimson-bramble army and servants of Arhallogen, but fought cautiously and kept their own losses low.
n.Highguard: The Valiant Pegasus crusaded in the Barrens under Achseh, hoping to repeat the successes of Zenith and to liberate the tribes held in subjugation by the Druj.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: scattered Great Forest Orcs were left in the Barrens when most of their sept fled south into Therunin.
n.The League: The Wolves of War advanced carefully under Jean Di Sarvos, supported by free companies from Holberg, and League scouts judged the Druj at least as numerous as the Imperial soldiers.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had been trapped in Zenith, turning the tables on the would-be tyrants of Urizen, and Urizen's armies are exempt from the conquest penalty in the Barrens.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle and Iron Helms pressed the Druj cautiously beside the Dawnish, pushing back the Causeway's borders and burning mounds of orc dead. Varushkan armies are exempt from the conquest penalty.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun marched from Sermersuaq to the Barrens.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: free companies recruited in Holberg supported the Wolves of War, whose general vowed to push the foe further from Holberg's walls.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun crossed from Sermersuaq to the Barrens with the help of Autumn magic.
t.The Barrens: The Steel Causeway held against a Druj counter-attack, and the Empire gained about a fifth of Bitter Strand at a cost of six thousand dead. The territory still festers under the Rivers Run Red curse and remains largely in Druj hands.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: most of the Great Forest Orc sept fled south from the Barrens into Therunin.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were trapped and broken in Zenith, where the Granite Pillar stayed behind to cleanse the remnants.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Bitter Strand was the focus of the Imperial advance. Its defences had been ruined by the storm, and the Druj ceded parts of the shoreline and fell back towards the damaged mithril mine at the Fangs.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: The ghulai's corrupting wards over the forests of Farweald struck at any Imperial forces that tried to push into the region.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Druj tried to recapture Hope's Rest, but the Imperial armies held it.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Saltmarsh lies drowned beneath the Bitter Sea after the summer's magical tempest, and is now coastal rather than marsh until at least the Summer Solstice.

Let the day die.d: The Greensward had stayed haunted since the bloody battles of 381YE, despite earlier efforts by the friars of Honour's Rest and Albert Fugglestone-Copperhill's priests. The Saker coven's Autumn Equinox enchantment calmed ghosts and helped the living understand them. Stories spread across the Mourn: some spirits found justice or rest, while a hateful spectre had to be destroyed. Friar John's call for aid was upheld but missed a greater majority, though some priests still came to Overton. Most remaining ghosts, human and orc, want to be remembered. The proposed Orchard of the Watch folly would cost 20 weirwood, 10 white granite and 60 crowns, take three months, and replace the haunted quality with memorial. If it were ever destroyed, the ghosts would rise furious.

n.Highguard: Highguard's Saker coven cast the Winter enchantment over the whole Mournwold that roused the ghosts and drew them closer to the living.
n.Jotun: Jotun ghosts from the Greensward battles fear the oblivion of the Howling Abyss and wish to be honoured. Mournwold thralls who understand some Jotun beliefs advised the priests on how to approach the orc dead.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr phantom led a friar to a shallow grave, and the remains are being carried north to Miaren.
n.The Marches: Marcher friars led the work to lay the Mourn's ghosts to rest, and the Marches may now build the Orchard of the Watch to quiet the Greensward dead for good.

t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the remains of a Navarr whose ghost was found in the Mourn are being taken to a final resting place in Miaren's glades.
t.Mournwold: The whole territory lay under the Saker enchantment, and ghostly encounters, both sorrowful and dangerous, spread across it before the magic began to fade.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The hateful spectre of a former owner drove everyone from the Hill-bridge Inn until the abbot and monks of Fordwater Monastery destroyed it and reclaimed the inn.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Mentioned in passing: in Freemoor a murderer was exposed by the weeping ghost of her dead lover, thanks to a brave governess.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: the ghosts of a long-dead company of soldiers paraded nightly through a Green March market town until the townsfolk came out to thank them.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Priests at Overton and Orchard's Watch found that the remaining ghosts want to be remembered. The proposed Orchard of the Watch would turn the region's haunted quality into a memorial one for as long as the trees stand.

Midnight rain.d: After the summer raid on Skallahn opened the Gullet to large numbers of ships, the Senate funded a project to chart the Sea of Snow. Captains from every nation except the Imperial Orcs took part, with roughly two-thirds being from Wintermark. The resulting map was not detailed enough for magicians, but it located the Narkyst territory of Ankashun, the Faraden territories of Menendram and Tujahan, and the Kalsea territories of Bryadvik, Tromsa and Fjorknae. Each fleet earned only modest returns from raiding and petty trade, plus a copy of the map and a gazetteer. Crews reported many kraken and other sea monsters. The findings were published after the Winter Solstice.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: three Dawnish captains, including Lord Romande Remys, are listed among the contributors.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: a single Highborn captain, Matthew, is listed among the contributors.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs were the only Imperial nation with no vessels involved in the project.
n.Jotun: The coasts of Kalsea and Narkyst were charted by Imperial ships, which also raided Jotun settlements, while the Jarls and their warriors drove off any crews who lingered or came ashore.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: two Navarr captains, Antur Longstep and Sylvan Blackleaf, are listed among the contributors.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: three Freeborn captains, including Aldo Russo, are listed among the contributors.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a single League captain, Erasmo di Tassato, is listed among the contributors.
n.The Marches: Around a dozen Marcher captains sailed with the expedition, the largest contingent after Wintermark, and each received a copy of the map and gazetteer.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a sailor's tall tale in the in-character story jokes about a Thule dragon riding a Summer dragon.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: two Urizen captains from Netherwatch are listed among the contributors.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk captains made up just over two-thirds of the fleets that mapped the Sea of Snow, braving kraken and hostile Jarls to chart the coast north of their homeland.

t.Bryadvik: The name and rough coastline of this Kalsea territory were charted for the first time by the Imperial expedition.
t.Fjorknae: Imperial captains recorded the name and rough coastline of this northern Kalsea territory.
t.Sea of Snow: Seventy or more Imperial fleets sailed these monster-haunted waters to map their shores, and many reported clashes with kraken and other beasts from the depths.
t.Skallahn: The earlier Imperial raids on this southernmost Kalsea territory, especially the damaging summer raid on the Kongegőr, opened the Gullet and made the mapping expedition possible.
t.Tromsa: The name and rough coastline of this Kalsea territory were mapped by the Imperial fleets.

Mime each lonely word.d: For a year, pilgrims who walk the Maze alone may emerge with new insight or purpose, though each person only once. Through the Law of Dominion the Guardian gained innate powers, including insight without liao, unique potions, unremovable personal auras and one oracular dream this year. The Thule ambassador Rak confirmed that the Dragon Hinodir of the Bright Orb holds Zoria's Staff of Pure Vision. He offered to sell it for exactly 120 thrones, 4 crowns and 11 rings, for one season only. The Maze's beasts speak in lucid dreams, letting the Guardian catalogue Varushka's sovereigns. Meanwhile the Wolves of Varushka grow more active, creating paid monster-hunting work for Varushkan and Dawnish forces.

n.Thule: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided confirmed that the Dragon Hinodir holds Zoria's Staff of Pure Vision and offered it for one season at an exact price. Any payment would be spent within the Empire on food sent north to the Thule.
n.Varushka: Varushka's Guardian gained unusual powers, its pilgrims could be transformed by the Maze, and dreams began to map its great sovereigns. Rising activity among the Wolves of Varushka also brought paid work for schlacta and wardens fighting monsters across the nation.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: some Suaq stories claim Zoria was a daughter of Sermersuaq who practised the lore of the icewalkers.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: characters who went to Brocéliande could not also have visited the Maze before the Winter Solstice.
t.Karov: More rusalka were reported in the rivers of Karov as the Wolves of Varushka grew more active.
t.Karsk: More dubik were reported active in the forests of Karsk, adding to the work for monster-hunting forces.
t.Miekarova: The consecrated Maze of Zoria in Miekarova drew growing numbers of pilgrims seeking a personal, transformative experience of Wisdom, an opportunity lasting until the Winter Solstice 385YE.
t.Ossium: More dubik were reported active in the forests of Ossium among the stirring Wolves of Varushka.
t.Otkodov: Legends hold that one of Zoria's relics fell into the hands of the Thule orcs of Otkodov in pre-Imperial times, and the Thule now confirm they hold her staff.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: characters who went to map the Sea of Snow could not also have visited the Maze before the Winter Solstice.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: some Suaq stories say Zoria was a daughter of Sermersuaq.
t.Volodmartz: More rusalka were reported in the rivers of Volodmartz, part of the growing monster threat facing Varushka.

r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Mentioned in passing: some of the Maze dreams were idle talk of snowfalls in the mountains of Miechernya.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: Mentioned in passing: some of the Maze dreams were gossip about a wedding in a vale in Brez.

No Peace.d: The Navarr Black Thorns, Isaella's Dance and Quiet Step, aided by servitors of Arhallogen, swept west through Gambit alongside the Brass Coast's Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs. The Lasambrians and Skjalderborn had already withdrawn in good order to Reinos, leaving only a few warbands and depots. Kahraman was liberated, but wrecked roads and bridges still crippled northern travel. In Bregasland the Strong Reeds and House Greywater kept up a guerrilla resistance while the Fishers courted the Bregas. In Liathaven, Jotun forces took every region except Liath's Heart, captured Hotter's Mire and slaughtered any Navarr they found. Four conjunctions offered chances to oppose Lasambrian raiders and Jotun patrols.

n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun gave up Kahraman and retreated to Reinos. Other Jotun upheld Mathilda Fisher's rule in Bregasland and conquered nearly all of Liathaven, planning a white granite citadel at Hotter's Mire.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns, Isaella's Dance and Quiet Step led the merciless sweep through Gambit. In Liathaven, however, the Jotun crushed the Navarr presence and executed any Navarr they caught, while the Blackroot Broker was asked to rescue Mott's apprentice.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs helped free Kahraman, with the Burning Falcons due to join next season. The nation now faces the costly task of repairing the shattered northern roads and protecting its mithril caravans from raiders.
n.The Marches: Bregasland remains under Fisher and Jotun rule, contested by the Strong Reeds and House Greywater, who need 10 thrones and 40 drams of herbs to continue. The fall of Liathaven left the Mournwold's people facing the Jotun at the threshold of the Mourn once more.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule cunning is credited, alongside Imperial strength, with driving the Jotun out of Sermersuaq.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not directly named; the page touches it only through the map's attachment of Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq is noted as free of the Jotun. In Kallavesa, Lasambrian raiders threatened a hylje settlement, and the Mediator of Hyljehal, Raal Dunn, was called on to drive them out.

t.Bregasland: Mathilda Fisher ruled from Fisher's Rock with Jotun backing and worked to win over the Bregas. The Strong Reeds lay low and House Greywater kept harrying the occupiers, though some households chose the quiet life.
t.Kahraman: The territory was wholly Imperial again after the Lasambrians withdrew. Sabotaged roads and bridges in the northern mountains, however, still crippled travel, and a Lasambrian warband planned to ambush mithril caravans from the Great Mine of Briante.
t.Kallavesa: A Lasambrian warband led by Sofio, calling themselves Hessar's Voice, marched near Rest to slaughter a hylje settlement on Lake Rikkivesi, threatening the Mediator of Hyljehal's mana crystal supply.
t.Liathaven: Jotun forces conquered every region except Liath's Heart, scattered the Feni and took Hotter's Mire as their base. They killed any Navarr they found, crushed Imperial steadings and stridings, and began dealing with the vallornspawn.
t.Mournwold: Navarr survivors fled into the Mournwold, whose farmers and miners now look west with dread, fearing a repeat of the earlier Jotun invasion of the Mourn.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not referred to anywhere on the page.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian armies retreated from Kahraman into the hills of Reinos.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are said to be gone from Sermersuaq, driven out by Imperial strength and Thule cunning.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Greywaters' harassment gave Grey Fens the allied insurgents quality. A Jotun force struck from here into West Ranging, and the Greywaters asked for supplies to be left at a copse in the south of the region.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Its garrison supported the Brass Coast armies, but destroyed roads and bridges badly hampered patrols and travel to the neighbouring mountain regions.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The five Imperial armies swept west across Gambit's dry plains, overcoming only straggling warbands and garrisoned depots. Diverted granite and mithril caravans now pass through it, exposed to bandits.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: Caravans of white granite and mithril must now detour south through Jade Range before heading east, increasing the risk from raiders and bandits.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Heralds of Cathan Canae descended from a conjured citadel here to aid the Fire of the South. Travel remains crippled, and a Lasambrian warband lay in ambush for the Great Mine of Briante's mithril caravans.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Passage through Serra Damata was brought to a standstill by the earlier destruction of roads and bridges, cutting it off from Serra Briante.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Mentioned in passing: West Marsh is not named; the Lasambrian raid in Kallavesa is placed near Rest and Lake Rikkivesi.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: The vallorn heart was the only part of Liathaven not in Jotun hands, though the few Imperial garrisons watching it were left isolated.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: The combined Jotun forces pushed east and captured Liath's Ring from the Feni, ending the recent uneasy détente there.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: This Feni region, part of the earlier détente, fell under Jotun control along with the rest of Liathaven. Duarte's Lasambrian warband set out from here to raid Kahraman.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: Jotun from Grey Fens smashed through West Ranging, crushing the Imperial garrisons and Navarr presence before using it as a base to push east.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: The Lasambrian Jotun came down from the Lasambrian Hills into Western Scout and quickly subdued it, along with the vallornspawn there.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: The Jotun overwhelmed the small Imperial presence and garrisons in Westwood, conquering the region.
r.Mournwold/Green March: A messenger expected at Green March never arrived, one of the first signs that Liathaven had fallen.

One last song.d: Heroes from every nation except the Imperial Orcs, aided by Great Forest Orcs and Highborn grey pilgrims, cleared the Druj from Elerael and Boar's Dell and set sentries along the borders. In Dark Ranging they slew a herald of Yaw'nagrah bound with the living heads of Heirs magicians. Others braved gardens of abomination for Spring-charged fruit. A weirwood Sanctuary Grove yielded the last singing stone, claimed by the Navarr. In Terunael explorers found a Wintermark-style runeforge, and some reached the vallornheart. The recovered lore will cut six months from the Great Library of Hacynian's vallorn research, if the library is built. The spent cauldron remains at the Broch.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: husks of Dawnish questing knights were found in the vallorn, and the Great Forest Orcs fought beside any Imperial force except perhaps the Dawnish.
n.Druj: Druj bands that had slipped into Brocéliande from the Barrens were scoured from Elerael and Boar's Dell by many small Imperial units, with scores killed and the rest fleeing east.
n.Highguard: Grey pilgrims and lay followers of the Way, urged on by a Highborn Assembly motion backed with liao, brought supplies and fighters to the assault on the Heirs' stronghold. Supporting congregations will receive herbs brought back by returning pilgrims.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: they were the only Imperial nation with no champions on the expedition.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but the last remnants of the Heirs of Terunael were said to be hiding in Liathaven, which they hold.
n.Navarr: Navarr champions led the exploration, kept Rhianos' cauldron at the Broch as a monument, and claimed the last singing stone of Terunael from the Sanctuary Grove. Some of their number became perhaps the first brands, thorns or vates ever to look upon a vallornheart.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn hero travelled all the way from Madruga to join the exploration.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League heroes who reached Terunael saw in the ruined city an echo of Sarvos and Temeschwar.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark heroes found a ruined building in western Terunael marked with Wintermark runes, holding what may be the remains of a runeforge like those of Skarsind and Gildenheim. Its presence there remains an unsolved mystery.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat farmers had reported Spring-steeped plants growing where the vallorn has touched, which raised the possibility of cultivating the vallorn fruit.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Highborn explorers saw in Terunael's ruin an echo of what could befall Bastion.
t.Brocéliande: Heroes swept the Druj from the territory, opened temporary paths through the vallorn and destroyed the last Heirs stronghold. They also explored the gardens of abomination, the Sanctuary Grove and the ruins of Terunael, carrying out great treasure and lore before withdrawing as Winter came.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea farmers had reported eerie Spring-steeped plants in vallorn-touched places, suggesting the fruit might be grown there.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Heirs of Terunael were earlier driven from Hercynia, and Great Forest Orcs had faced abominations there.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the last scattered Heirs of Terunael hide in Liathaven, and the weirwood sanctuary recalled one found when the Westwood was cleansed.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn hero came from Madruga to join the expedition.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: no Navarr had looked upon a vallornheart since the destruction of Miaren's.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold farmers had spoken of Spring-steeped plants in vallorn-touched places, where the vallorn fruit might be cultivated.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: it appears only in further reading, through a later expedition to Bendol.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: League heroes saw in ruined Terunael an echo of Sarvos.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the runeforge-like ruin in Terunael struck explorers as eerily reminiscent of the runeforge beneath Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Terunael's walls, when whole, would have equalled those of modern Temeschwar.
t.The Barrens: Druj had been slipping into Brocéliande from the Barrens, and the survivors fled back east towards it. New sentry posts now watch the border.
t.Therunin: The Senator for Therunin rallied the Great Forest Orcs who now live in Therunin, and their hunters, scouts and healers fought alongside the Imperial heroes.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: The Broch in Black Boughs was the expedition's base, where the heralds of Rhianos served the cauldron's soup. The spent cauldron remains there in Navarr keeping as a monument.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The Druj were driven out of Boar's Dell with help from Great Forest Orcs who once lived there. Sentries now watch its borders, and a path through the vallorn links it to Elerael.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: The hidden Heirs of Terunael stronghold in Dark Ranging was stormed and its castellan, a herald of Yaw'nagrah bound with living Heirs magicians, was destroyed. The woven fortress then unravelled.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael was cleared of Druj and guarded with sentry posts, and paths were carved so small groups could pass safely to Boar's Dell or the Broch.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Explorers breached the ruined city of Terunael, finding the Wintermark-style runeforge and a mysterious step-pyramid. Some pressed on to look upon the vallornheart itself.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: A battlefield in eastern Vale's Lament, where Highborn and Heirs had destroyed each other, yielded clues that led to the Heirs' hidden stronghold.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn-free weirwood grove recalled a similar discovery made when the Westwood was cleansed.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: it appears only in further reading, through a later report of an expedition to Bendol.

Raise fourth Wintermark army.d: The motion was framed as fulfilling Wintermark's ambition to field a fourth army, with the proposer reminding other nations of the support he had given their own military levies. The commission required 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones and would take a year to complete. Hengest Dun supplied most of the materials across several seasons from Winter Solstice 384YE to Winter Solstice 385YE, with smaller contributions from Lumi Warmthbringer, Farren Silver Streams, Corwyn Heartsbane and Arlen Frostmire. Once complete, a fourth Wintermark army would be raised. If the smokehouse of Atalaq had been built at least six months before mustering finished, the army would be offered qualities in line with the Suaq tradition without further opportunities.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark secured Senate approval to field a fourth army, achieving a stated national ambition, with Hengest Dun and other Wintermark citizens largely funding the mithril and money required.

t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the motion cited the consecration of the Kallavesa marshes as support for raising the new army.
t.Sermersuaq: The new fourth Wintermark army was to be raised in Sermersuaq, whose senator seconded the motion, and it could gain Suaq-tradition qualities if the smokehouse of Atalaq was completed in time.

Ratify treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact.d: Proposed by Reikos and seconded by Volodmartz, the treaty would have set three years of peace with Grendel residing in or operating from Spiral, with renegotiation after two years and a 50-mithril break clause. Spiral would have stayed uncontested, and no Grendel forces would have moved through it into Imperial land. Kaliact's people would have refused trade with and aid to the Druj, the north Mareave trading consortium would have offered better rates, and Kaliact would have provided a fort-construction ritual text and 10 wains of mithril. The Senate rejected it. The Constitutional Court warned that its activation clause could only work by letting the Ambassador announce treaties without a Senate vote.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the treaty would have barred Kaliact and those in Spiral from trading with the Druj or giving them material help against the Empire without Imperial leave.
n.Grendel: Salt Lord Kaliact's proposed separate peace with the Empire, which offered mithril, a ritual text and trade concessions, was rejected by the Senate.

t.Mareave: The treaty would have had the north Mareave trading consortium offer the Empire improved rates on several resources, but this did not happen because the treaty was rejected.
t.Spiral: The rejected treaty would have kept Spiral uncontested, barred Grendel forces from attacking the Empire through it, and protected the treatment of law-abiding Imperial citizens living there.

Reconstruct Golden Cascade.d: The motion passed at 200 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Mournwold. The reconstruction required 60 wains of weirwood, 15 thrones and six months' work. Cadeus supplied the 15 thrones and 44 wains of weirwood after the Winter Solstice 384YE and the remaining 16 wains after the Spring Equinox 385YE. With the work complete, the Golden Cascade provides a share of 100 random herbs to farms and 30 crowns to herb gardens in Zenith. It also gives a significant boost to food supply across Urizen, allowing the nation to keep fully supplying the Citadel Guard indefinitely, provided Urizen retains all three of its current territories.

n.Urizen: The rebuilt Golden Cascade boosts food supply across Urizen, letting the nation fully supply the Citadel Guard indefinitely so long as it holds all three of its current territories.

t.Zenith: Zenith regains the Golden Cascade, whose output shares 100 random herbs among the territory's farms and 30 crowns among its herb gardens.

r.Zenith/Proceris: The Golden Cascade was rebuilt in Proceris over six months using 60 wains of weirwood and 15 thrones, both supplied by Cadeus.

Reconstruct Starlight Drift of Shimmerin.d: The commission cost 6 wains of mithril and 7 thrones, with three months needed to complete it. It was funded piecemeal across several seasons. Felix of the Wise Citadel, Nathair Autumngale and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov each gave a crown after the Winter Solstice 384YE. Peregrinus, Serenus Starsong and Nathair Autumngale gave further crowns after the Spring Equinox 385YE. Crassus then provided the 6 wains of mithril and 6 thrones 1 crown after the Summer Solstice 385YE, finishing the work. With the sinecure complete, the Urizen title of Custodian of the Starlight Drift became available to appoint from the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen gained a new national title, the Custodian of the Starlight Drift, which became available to appoint from the Autumn Equinox 385YE once the mana sinecure was finished.

t.Zenith: A mana sinecure was built at Endsmeet in Zenith, which was held by Urizen. It was paid for over several seasons and completed after the Summer Solstice 385YE.

r.Zenith/Occursion: Occursion became home to the Starlight Drift of Shimmering Snow, a mana sinecure at Endsmeet commissioned in the wake of the Write your own ending Wind of Fortune.

Scuppernong.d: The vines grew from Gawain's effort after Timinion Splitroot's death in 381YE to organise Navarr healers. Enis Splinterspear's statement, passed by greater majority, asked the egregores to walk the trods with the message. Steadings and stridings were intrigued but raised three questions. Who bears the costs of herbs and mana? Who should be healed, including foreigners and barbarians? What do vines heal: the maladies of the world, or making people stronger? An egregore will attend the vines' meeting at the next summit to seek agreed answers. Anything affecting how other Navarr treat vines would need a further Assembly statement. Separately, Avery Farkas will gather vines and thorns to rescue missing Marchers in Brocéliande.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Maire of the Leaping Salmon Steading asks whether a Druj slave is truly her enemy when arguing that vines might heal anyone.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel paymaster appears in Imma Heartshrew's triage dilemma, and Maire asks whether a Grendel merchant is an enemy.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Maire's suggestion that vines might treat wounded Jotun, to address the cycle of killing between Jotun and Navarr, provoked considerable anger.
n.Navarr: The egregores carried news of the vines to every steading and striding, and the nation now awaits answers from Anvil on funding, whom to heal and the vines' guiding philosophy before the vines can become a true Navarr archetype like guides, brands and vates.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: securing a lasting peace between the Thule and the Empire is offered as an example of the kind of malady a vine might seek to heal.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character notes cite recent Urizen archetype pages, such as architect and sword scholar, as models for what a vines archetype would need.

t.Brocéliande: A conjunction leads into the depths of Brocéliande, where Avery Farkas will gather vines and thorns to rescue a band of Marchers trapped by a danger other than the vallorn, after many champions pushed into the forest last season.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: a physick treating the sick in a surgery in Miaren is cited as someone for whom battlefield-focused vine practices matter little.

r.Brocéliande/Elerael: A band of Marcher champions went missing along the northern borders of Elerael, apparently caught by a malignant threat other than the vallorn, and Navarr volunteers are called to reach them through the Sentinel Gate.

Shake it off.d: The Conclave rejected Meraud's offer but backed Sadogua's plan and dropped the requirement that refugees convert to the Way. Sadogua sought 100 to 200 crystal mana. That sum would fall if Drawing the Penumbral Veil were cast on Segura and Madruga, or if a Declaration of Concord urged magicians to settle refugees far from the border. The outcomes depended on how much was raised. Barien asked the Weigher of Worth to challenge Jarl Roneth. Callidus, Wise Rangara and Zakalwe issued invitations, and Ylenrith asked for a parley. Five more Black Drop rituals entered Urizen lore, and the last of the Black Drop's Childer was found murdered in Kahraman.

n.Dawn: Zakalwe's lieutenant Agon was to visit the Dawnish camp to pick five strategists for a Spring Equinox game based on Empress Brannan's failed Barrens campaign. Wise Rangara also wanted Safir du Cercle of Dawn at her meeting and hinted at foolishness to come in Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe is said to have aided Imperial heroes against the Druj, and his strategy game draws on Brannan's failed conquest of the Barrens.
n.Grendel: Sadogua's proposed cunning mist would let him guide fleeing Suranni magicians through Grendel-held Feroz, though his heralds would not explain how.
n.Jotun: Jarl Roneth of Overgaard was carrying an ancestral sword recovered from Lake Lansipari back towards Skallahn. Barien asked the Weigher of Worth to give the Jarl's Ulfur and their Cathan Canae heralds a harder fight on the way.
n.Navarr: Sadogua named the peripatetic Navarr as one of the preferred refuges for Suranni magicians. A Navarr was also among the three strangers who met the murdered Black Drop member in Kahraman.
n.The Brass Coast: Segura and Madruga were the proposed sites for a Night-magic shroud to hide Suranni refugees crossing the border. Separately, Jodeya Watiker, the last of the Black Drop's Childer, was found murdered in a Kahraman parador.
n.Urizen: Five more illegal Black Drop rituals calling on Agramant entered Urizen lore, to the discomfort of Phaleron's attendants. Barien's heralds were also to hold court at the Scarlet Guard's tent.
n.Varushka: Sadogua suggested Varushka as one of the places where Suranni refugee magicians might find safe homes far from the Iron Confederacy's reach.
n.Wintermark: Sadogua suggested Wintermark as one of the places where Suranni refugee magicians might settle safely, far from Suranni lawkeepers.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named; the page refers only to refugees taking a ship north to reach the Empire.
t.Feroz: If the cunning mist were woven, Sadogua said it would let him guide fleeing Suranni magicians through Feroz by means his heralds would not explain.
t.Kahraman: Jodeya Watiker di Tassato Mestra, the last known member of the Black Drop's Childer, was found dead in Kahraman. Her killers appear to have come and gone through the Sentinel Gate from Anvil.
t.Madruga: Sadogua proposed that Drawing the Penumbral Veil be cast on Madruga at magnitude 24 or more, so he could weave a mist hiding Suranni refugees from Confederacy pursuers.
t.Segura: Segura was one of the two border territories where Sadogua wanted Drawing the Penumbral Veil cast at magnitude 24 or more to shroud fleeing Suranni magicians.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is not named on the page; any link is likely Jarl Roneth's journey from Lake Lansipari towards Skallahn.
t.Skallahn: Jarl Roneth was making for the border of Skallahn to return the recovered sword to Overgaard, while the Weigher of Worth was asked to challenge the Jarl's force before it got there.
t.The Barrens: Zakalwe's planned strategy game draws on Empress Brannan's failed attempt to conquer the Barrens in 257YE, and Agon wished to hear about Dawn's current war of conquest there.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Irontide Wessek is said to have died on the battlefield in Zenith, and Bartimaeus of Zenith Ascendant was summoned to a meeting arranged by Callidus.

r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The body of the last Black Drop member was found in The Gecko's Nest, a parador in the Jade Range. She died after meeting a Marcher, a Navarr and an Urizeni.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Mentioned in passing: Iron Stand is not named; any link is Jarl Roneth's journey to return the sword to Overgaard in Skallahn.

Snow might fall.d: The Rime Hammer was recovered, the Gildenheim runeforge ruins moved to Runegrott and Barien's challenge completed. This cut the runeforge's cost to 30 wains each of white granite and mithril and 60 of weirwood, with no labour costs and a year to build. When the Thule Dragons outlawed slavery, the artisans taken from Skarsind in 373YE were freed, and most settled at Runegrott. If the Wintermark National Assembly sends a priest with true liao to consecrate the caves as an inspirational tomb for Isenbrad, locals would give fifteen wains of weirwood. The freed smiths would also establish the Runesmith's Law, seven unique magic items that only Wintermark artisans could make. The opportunity remained open, and it did not depend on the runeforge being built.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the only link is the word 'spiral', used for the ice pillars at Runegrott and for the Spiral Sword in Redoubt.
n.Imperial Orcs: Gildenheim now lies in Imperial orc lands, which is why most of the returning artisans settled at Runegrott instead. A further runeforge opportunity involving the Ethengraw sept of orcs is described in a separate wind.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Thule raid on the forges at Treji in Hercynia is recalled as the place where several masters of runic lore were captured.
n.Thule: The Thule Dragons' outlawing of slavery secured the release of the Wintermark runesmiths their armies had captured and forced to labour in Otkodov.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the building of the Spiral Sword in Redoubt may have inspired Wintermark, and the Runesmith's Law is likened to the unique knowledge held by the Urizeni.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark stood close to reclaiming its place as home of the greatest artisans. It had a cheaper runeforge within reach and a National Assembly mandate available to consecrate Isenbrad's tomb, which would unlock the nation-only Runesmith's Law.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is the proposed site of the Runegrott runeforge, which would also create a Wintermark national position. Most of the freed artisans have settled there.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Thule raid on the forges at Treji in Hercynia, during the fall of Skarsind, is where several runic masters were taken.
t.Otkodov: The captured Wintermark runesmiths were held as slaves in Otkodov until the Thule ended slavery, and they have now left for home.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the building of the Spiral Sword in Redoubt is suggested as an inspiration for Wintermark's runeforge ambitions.
t.Skarsind: The Thule conquest of Skarsind and Gildenheim in 373YE is what robbed Wintermark of its runesmiths. Gildenheim's ruined runeforge has now been moved to Runegrott.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; 'spiral' appears only to describe the Runegrott ice pillars and the Spiral Sword in Redoubt.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: The rune-carved ice caves of Runegrott beneath Northspires are where the runeforge would be built and where Isenbrad's tomb could be consecrated with true liao.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: The workshops of Nithoggir were where the enslaved Wintermark runesmiths were forced to toil before their release.

The money goes round.d: Building on the new Chair of the Wolf and Aureliana di Sarvos's Spring Equinox Assembly call for a city to be first to 100 Thrones in tax, Fransesca reworked the idea. The winner will be the city where the most wains are spent on commissions and personal resources between the Winter Solstice 384YE and the 385YE solstice; Imperial armies do not count. The civil service will publish a seasonal 'League table'. For the year, upgrading business resources in the League costs one wain of white granite less. Nine opportunities, many previously lapsed, can be commissioned until the end of the Autumn Equinox 385YE. They include sea defences, a cathedral and a university renovation in Sarvos, a Colossus of Tassato and a University of Temeschwar.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the revived Holmauer fortifications were originally proposed in 380YE as defences designed to kill the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the uncertain Grendel peace treaty is cited as a reason for Sarvos sea defences, and the Grendel are noted as having looted Capodomus Cathedral.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: a restored Capodomus Cathedral is said to rival the Basilica of Seven Doors in Bastion.
n.The League: The League's four cities are pitted against each other for a year to prove which is greatest through investment. League businesses gain cheaper upgrades, and several commission opportunities are now open in League territories.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: its Basilica of Seven Doors is the benchmark that a restored Capodomus Cathedral would rival.
t.Holberg: Holberg competes as one of the four cities and can pursue revived opportunities for lethal new fortifications at Holmauer and the Duelling Field Gardens.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos has the most revived opportunities. These are sea defences, the Diora University renovation with a College of Autumn Magic, the restoration of Capodomus Cathedral, the Glass Palace and Greatest Taste follies, and a firehouse.
t.Tassato: Tassato competes as one of the four cities and could commission the Colossus of Tassato, a giant statue on the Red Rock meant to outdo the Colossus of Sarvos.
