t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar competes as one of the four cities, and the proposed University of Temeschwar remains available until Summer 385YE.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Brechtje Van Holberg's 380YE plan to add deadly defences against the Druj at Holmauer is available again. So is a proposal to turn the old Duelling Society field in Holmauer Park into a magical herb garden.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mentioned in passing: Fransesca describes herself as running some of the least prestigious gambling houses in Tassato Mestra.

The silent page.d: After seizing the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest and repelling a Druj counter-attack, the Empire chose to send messages of hope rather than take the Fangs. The Highborn Assembly, and thanks to the Gryphon's Pride's orders also the Dawn Assembly, could each mandate an approach to one faction: the Great Forest Orcs, Black Wind, Vendarri, Montanians, Karass or Barrens Dawnish. A successful approach would let generals meet that faction's representatives. Three competing mandates were offered: the Way and Lenarius Ankarien's versions would boost casualties against the Druj by a fifth, while Fintan Nighthaven's would penalise generals urging "Death to the Druj". The tepel Varag Soulflayer, torturing Montanian captives in the Untrod Groves, fell to the Champion of Vigilance to kill.

n.Dawn: The Gryphon's Pride under the late Garravaine De Rondell pushed into the Barrens, opening a chance for the Dawn Assembly to mandate an approach to a faction. The Dawnish yeofolk still living under Druj rule were eager to help but wary of Imperial politics over the territory's future.
n.Druj: The Druj were driven back from Hope's Rest and the Carmine Fields and faced Imperial efforts to turn their subject peoples against them. They also faced possible mandates calling for their outright extermination, while their tepel Varag Soulflayer threatened to unleash tortured souls on Imperial armies.
n.Highguard: The Valiant Pegasus committed itself wholly to a crusade to liberate the Barrens, giving the Highborn Assembly the opportunity to mandate an approach to one of six Barrens factions. Highborn wayfarers and grey pilgrims would find the Great Forest Orcs the easiest to reach.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's relationship with the Great Forest Orcs settled in Therunin was noted to have slowly improved.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar was to remain in Zenith to clear the Druj remnants, and the Druj destruction of Zenith's libraries was invoked as a reason for vengeance.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Karass of the Barrens were believed to be distant kin of the Menrothat sept in Ossium.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Menrothat sept here was said to be related to the Karass and to have had a similar relationship with the Druj.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Druj torture of the people of Reikos was cited as a reason for the cry "Death to the Druj".
t.The Barrens: Imperial armies held the line here rather than conquer outright, seeking to win over its six rival factions against the Druj. A tepel's camp in the territory threatened 500 additional casualties among Imperial armies unless the Champion of Vigilance acted.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs who fled the Barrens were settled here by treaty on condition they help defend it, and most of their leadership dwells here.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar would stay to cleanse Druj remnants, and the despoiling of its libraries was invoked against the Druj.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Imperial forces advanced towards the Fangs, the vital mithril resource here, but chose not to take them. The Black Wind orcs, once based around the Fangs, now fight for the Druj out of hatred for the Empire.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The remaining Great Forest Orcs in the Barrens dwell mostly here, a weak faction but the easiest for Imperial envoys to approach.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Hope's Rest was captured by the Imperial attack, and surviving Montanians scattered into the surrounding mountains offered to show the Empire "how to make swords".
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish yeofolk still living here were among those the Empire could approach.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The secretive and pragmatic Vendarri orcs dwell here, their home flooded by storms on the Bitter Sea; they might be persuaded to switch sides while victory over the Druj seems likely.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: The tepel Varag Soulflayer had set up camp here with arkad troops to turn captured Montanians into tortured souls, and the Champion of Vigilance was responsible for killing him.

The two of us.d: Dawn's enchanters have until the Summer Solstice to choose and agree terms with Summer eternals. Eleonaris stands ready and would resent being passed over; Hayaak refuses outright, demanding the head of the long-dead Ser Edric du Gauvain; most others want a giant statue, while Adamant has offered an alternative through the Master of the Koboldi. Jaheris will not share patronage with Eleonaris, but would accept her existing statue being magically altered to depict him for a year, at the cost of her wrath falling on someone. Alternatively, Dawn could turn wholly to Winter eternals, which Eleonaris would ignore. The egregores proposed a meeting at 2pm on Saturday to decide.

n.Dawn: Dawn's enchanters and enchantresses must decide whether to court the Summer eternals, try the Jaheris statue gambit or switch entirely to Winter to secure patrons for the Eastern Sky, with their egregores calling a meeting to settle the matter.
n.Jotun: Rumour holds that the Jotun jarls declined the Gryphon-King's free offer as a likely trap, only grudgingly allowing a handful of his heralds to take the field with their kirkja after the Queen of Glory took offence.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is cited as a place where Night magic has reportedly changed a statue's appearance at least twice before.

t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is noted as where Night magic has apparently altered statues at least twice, as precedent for disguising Eleonaris' statue as Jaheris.

Two silhouettes.d: The first battle option targeted Sarra Grubfeast, the brutal Druj governor of Dawnguard, at the de Challon Estate. Its objectives were to kill her, capture the declared sorcerer Renee du Loire, and deal with the Venom Weavers coven and tortured fallen knights. The second, via the Sentinel Gate to Bitterhead near The Fangs, aimed to rescue surviving Rahvin orcs, ideally without Dawnish diplomats, and to threaten a summer regio. Three conjunctions were also offered. One would stop the Bone Serpent clan bringing a herald to destroy the Palace of Orieb. Another would halt the Burnt Fist coven heading for the weirwood of the Eaves of Peytaht. A third would stop Garsnag Mudchurner slaughtering Dawnish partisans.

n.Dawn: Dawnish yeofolk in Dawnguard suffered under Sarra Grubfeast, and killing her would lift Dawnish morale and remove the risk of the region being sacked. The Rahvin hated the Dawnish, so Dawn could fight at Bitterhead but should not join any talks with them.
n.Druj: The Druj were offered as targets on several fronts: Grubfeast and her council, the Bitterhead mithril workings and their Rahvin slaves, and the Bone Serpent, Screaming Wasp and Garsnag Mudchurner forces.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Druj burning of spires and slaughter of their occupants in Zenith was cited as an example of Druj despoiling.
n.Varushka: Scouts of the Northern Eagle spotted the Bone Serpent clan escorting the Sleepless Nightmare towards the Palace of Orieb. Responsibility for the conjunction fell to the Apothecary of Orieb, Nikolai Desovich Patazca, unless the Varushkan Senators appointed a successor first.

t.Astolat: Elation in Astolat over the Steel Causeway risked turning to frustration as news of Dawnguard's suffering spread, and killing Grubfeast would quiet the most impatient voices.
t.Ossium: The Bone Serpent clan, driven from Ossium almost two years earlier, was moving towards its border with a herald able to destroy the Palace of Orieb.
t.Semmerholm: Public mood in Semmerholm risked souring over the plight of Dawnguard's people, and a strike on Grubfeast would help consolidate support for the Imperial strategy.
t.The Barrens: The territory was split by the Iron Causeway, and every option on the page lay here: the Dawnguard governor, the Bitterhead mine and Rahvin, the Peytaht weirwood and the Murderdale partisans.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater's joy at the Steel Causeway victory risked becoming frustration at the brutal conditions in Dawnguard, which killing the governor would help ease.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: cited as where the Druj burned spires and slaughtered their occupants simply to damage the Empire.

r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: If the Bone Serpent group crossed the border into Drownbark Forest, it would be lost to Imperial eyes and the Palace of Orieb would fall.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Imperial armies were pressing into Bitter Strand, where heroes could strike at Bitterhead by The Fangs to free the Rahvin from a woodland stockade near the Druj mithril mine and threaten a summer regio.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: The Bone Serpent clan's elite warriors and Vikari were escorting the Sleepless Nightmare through Farweald towards the Ossium border.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Burnt Fist coven was heading for the Eaves of Peytaht to enchant weirwood workers. Stopping it would hamper Druj harvesting for at least a season and let scouts recover wains of weirwood.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Recently conquered as part of the Iron Causeway, Hope's Rest was where a coven holding the Bitterhead regio could summon one of Cathan Canaes's Frozen Citadels.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Murderdale had no significant Druj military presence, but Garsnag Mudchurner's clan was retreating towards the lands of House de Percy to slaughter its partisans.

Watching my mistakes.d: The Wintermark Assembly had settled that former thralls could reweave their skeins, but many resistance fighters had survived through pacts with Blood-on-the-Snow. Four non-exclusive options, open only during the Winter Solstice, were set out: a Senate motion for sweeping magistrate investigations, costing Sermersuaq's military units two ranks for two seasons; a Synod investigation by the Silent Bell; a Conclave declaration sending the Shuttered Lantern to study the Howler's boons; or a Wintermark Assembly mandate sending priests to seek out offenders. Monsters from Agramant and Hayaak also roamed the territory. The proposed Hall of the Hunters (12 white granite, 3 thrones) would yield 9 mana and a monster-hunting paid work option.

n.Jotun: The Jotun have been driven from Sermersuaq, leaving behind their castles, thousands of cairns and the rune-carved stone markers that failed to keep the Howler's monsters out.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the opening story's Wintermark hunter bought her wolf-hound from a dog-training shop in Holberg.
n.Thule: The Thule warlocks gathered at Tanikipari were massacred by Hayaak's followers in Autumn 384YE, and the Griffon-King's monsters then scattered across Sermersuaq.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark is whole again but must decide how to deal with Winterfolk who made pacts with Blood-on-the-Snow; its Assembly could send priests to root them out and appoint a Banner-Bearer of Atkonaroq if the Hall of the Hunters is built.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: some Wintermarkers escaped the Jotun conquest of Sermersuaq by fleeing to Hahnmark.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the hound in the opening story was bought from a dog-training shop in Holberg.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: some Wintermarkers escaped the Jotun conquest of Sermersuaq by fleeing to Kallavesa.
t.Sermersuaq: Back under Imperial control, Sermersuaq faces possible investigations into cultists of Blood-on-the-Snow and is troubled by Winter and Summer monsters that a proposed Hall of the Hunters could keep at bay.

r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Mentioned in passing: the respected Kallavesi magistrate Heorl Thunderspeaker, based in Sealtoq, could conduct any trials arising from a Wintermark Assembly mandate.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Hall of the Hunters was proposed for the shore of Lake Atkonaroq in the Suaq Wastes, as a base for heroes hunting the monsters of Blood-on-the-Snow and Hayaak, producing 9 mana a season.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Hayaak's army slaughtered the Thule warlocks gathered at Tanikipari in Autumn 384YE, and his monsters afterwards scattered across the territory rather than returning to the Summer realm.

We are never ever getting back together.d: Rachensgrab yielded ten fleets, now being repaired in Sarvos, and two ritual texts, all held by Fleet Admiral Abel of Zenith Ascendant. Asavea remained at war with the Empire, and Jarm had severed ties. The Grendel embassy was completed. Salt Lord Kaliact of Spiral sent Speaker Curstag to Anvil to discuss renegotiating the peace treaty, and a Grendel navy anchored off Necropolis. The Vandersaar offered an Alivetti Market in Cigno, while the Gjullit family offered regular weirwood through altered or new docks. Three Lawkeeper knights came to work with the militia against the Hand of Dumon. Mathilda Fisher's terms for a Free Nation of Bregas were restated. The Senate had also amended tariffs on several foreign nations.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Lord Colwynn de Rondell of Dawn is named as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, and Jarrigk Orzel of Dawn as the Imperial Consul who met Mathilda Fisher.
n.Grendel: The Grendel faced Imperial sanctions even as their embassy was completed and Salt Lord Kaliact sought talks on the peace treaty. One of their navies was also anchored off Necropolis, and a Grendel in Nemoria bought the Temple of the Noble Virtues' idol of Prosperity.
n.Highguard: The National Assembly of Highguard was asked for a Statement of Principle on trading with the Grendel sailors in Necropolis, which would decide whether local businesses profited. Accalon of Felix's Watch also served as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs is named as Ambassador to Asavea, which is now at war with the Empire.
n.Jotun: Any treaty with Mathilda Fisher would require the Jotun to withdraw their armies from Bregasland and lose the Fishers' support. Harald Longaxe attended the Anvil meeting on behalf of Gudmundur Arason.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Gelert Ashborn of Navarr is named as Ambassador to Jarm, which has severed ties with the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn figured prominently. Esteban and Ezro were invited to the Grendel negotiations, some Freeborn plotted to steal the Scorrero Nets, and the Gjullit suggested new weirwood docks to serve a Brass Coast navy.
n.The League: Sarvos received the ten captured fleets and was named as the site of the proposed Vandersaar market, which League traders could use through a Trademaster. Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato served as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.
n.Thule: The Senate moved trade with the Thule first from sanctions and then to free trade as reparation for Thunderous Deluge, and the Empire was said to have secured significant change in Thule society.
n.Urizen: Urizen figures were central. Abel of Zenith Ascendant held the Rachensgrab spoils, Urizeni served as ambassadors to the Sarcophan Delves and Axos, and the Urizen encampment was suggested for the Grendel talks.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Gjullit family proposed that the Senate could build entirely new docks anywhere along the Bay of Catazar to receive regular weirwood shipments, an offer the Senate had not yet taken up.
t.Bregasland: Mathilda Fisher still controlled Bregasland and sought a treaty making it an independent nation, with the Strong Reeds and the Jotun armies both withdrawing. An attempt by Marchers to assassinate her at Anvil had failed.
t.Necropolis: At least one Grendel navy anchored off Necropolis and its sailors frequented local taverns. If Highguard endorsed trading with them, Necropolis business owners would gain extra income before the Spring Equinox.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the nations whose tariffs the Senate amended the previous season.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Sejanus, the Senator for Redoubt, was invited to the negotiations with Salt Lord Kaliact's representatives.
t.Sarvos: The ten fleets taken at Rachensgrab were being repaired by the Sarvos Shipwrights Syndicate, but no Asavean merchants came to Sarvos's markets or the Cavabianca Dock.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra, the Senator for Segura, attended the meeting with Mathilda Fisher.
t.Spiral: Salt Lord Kaliact of Spiral had profited from a year of trade with the Empire and sent Speaker Curstag to Anvil to discuss renegotiating the peace treaty. The Spiral Envoy was among those invited.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Fleet Admiral Abel's name, Abel of Zenith Ascendant, is the only reference to Zenith.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mentioned in passing: the North Fens are not named specifically; the page discusses Bregasland as a whole under Mathilda Fisher.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: The Vandersaar proposed the Alivetti Market in Cigno, at an old villa with a decaying dock. It would need ten wains of weirwood, 20 crowns and three months to build, and would create a Trademaster able to buy ingots and measures.

Wildest dreams.d: Donations, including from Mournwold orcs, funded the Black Canal between Meade and Sarcombe, but it stalled for want of white granite and weirwood. For a year, ministries commissioned in Sarcombe would cost less. The Chestnut Cartel proposed an Alder of Sarcombe sinecure. Clearing Alderly could support a fifth Marcher army after a year, which mattered because losing Bregasland left the four existing armies close to the limit of supply. Proposed commissions included New Longstwick Market, a deep lift at the Singing Caves and Green Iron Hill. Stephen of Sarcombe remained at large. In two conjunctions, the Bailiff of the Downs had to stop Little Robin reaching Liathaven, and the Master of Sarcombe Metal Market had to rescue Wise Maggie from Jotun raiders.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard traders are occasionally seen in Sarcombe's markets haggling for fine metals.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces held Bregasland and were massing in Liathaven, threatening the Mournwold and Mitwold. A raiding party under Jarl Hyglak the Quarrelsome hunted a Sarcombe metal merchant, and Jotun escorts awaited the traitor Little Robin.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast merchants are common visitors to Sarcombe, and Kahraman miners might be drawn to work the deep veins of the Singing Caves.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: merchants from Tassato frequent Sarcombe, which also offers markets for the fine goods of League cities.
n.The Marches: The Marches were offered a canal, new titles and ministries in the Mournwold, and a route to supporting a fifth army. However, with Bregasland lost, its four armies would begin to deteriorate if it lost one more region of Upwold or Mitwold, or two regions of the Mournwold.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan traders are occasionally seen in Sarcombe's markets buying fine metals.

t.Bregasland: Under Jotun control, Bregasland's fens no longer supported the Marcher armies. The Strong Reeds were harrying the Jotun and Mathilda Fisher, while Stephen of Sarcombe's people worked with the Fishers to sway the Bregas folk.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe fought in the Kahraman campaign, leading forces at Rojota and ruining its roads, and Kahraman miners might be hired for the Singing Caves.
t.Liathaven: Jotun were massing in Liathaven once again, a raiding party slipped over the border from there into the Mournwold, and the traitor Little Robin was trying to reach it to pass on intelligence.
t.Mitwold: Meade was the planned terminus of the stalled Black Canal, and Jotun armies stood on Mitwold's threshold, with only the marshes of Oddmire between them and Meade. Losing a single region here would leave the Marcher armies without enough supply.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold prospered around Sarcombe and was offered several opportunities: a canal, civic offices, the clearance of Alderly, deep mining and a green iron outpost. It also faced Jotun raids and the traitor Little Robin, and losing two of its regions would leave the Marcher armies without enough supply.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named; the page refers only to occasional Varushkan traders in Sarcombe.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato merchants are common visitors to Sarcombe, and its miners might be attracted to the deep veins of the Singing Caves.
t.Upwold: The presence of orc labourers on the canal raised eyebrows in Upwold, and losing a single Upwold region would leave all four Marcher armies without enough supply.

Write the lines.d: The Jotun ruled Sermersuaq harshly but did not lay it waste. The opportunities were: finishing the Smokehouse of Atalaq to support Wintermark's planned fourth, Suaq army (open until Autumn 384YE); completing the Jotun expansion of the Pride of Ikka's Tears and improving its supply route; renaming, remodelling or decommissioning Olgafsdottirshal and the Fortress of Kalant; and two Thule offers from Warlock Askja of Volham, a food-for-ilium trading hall at Wreck and five-year hunting rights, available only at the Winter Solstice. Jarl Ragnar the Dour was leading Ulfur and heralds towards Kalant to wreck the surrounding roads and bridges. Intercepting him fell to the Senator of Sermersuaq.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were cited as a contrast, a people who leave devastation behind and might have collapsed the mine out of spite.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had collapsed the pass linking southern Sermersuaq to Skarsind.
n.Jotun: The Jotun's unfinished works and fortresses were left for the Empire to complete, rename or abandon, and renaming them was expected to be taken as a calculated insult. Meanwhile Jarl Ragnar of Peråsen led Ulfur and heralds of Cathan Canae towards the Fortress of Kalant.
n.Thule: Weakened by Hayaak's slaughter of their warlocks and short of food since the Dragons freed their slaves, the Thule offered ilium for food caravans through a trading hall at Wreck. They also offered up to 30 rings of ilium for five years of hunting rights in Suaq Fount and East Floes.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark was presented with the means to raise a fourth army rooted in Suaq tradition through the Smokehouse of Atalaq, and could rename the Jotun fortresses by statement of principle. It also had to weigh the Thule's offers of ilium for food and hunting rights.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark was named as the soul of the Steinr tradition, as a comparison for Sermersuaq's place in Suaq identity.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's swamps were consecrated to Pride with true liao by Rane Sherarding, and this is what allows Wintermark to support a fourth army. The territory was also described as the spiritual heart of the Kallavesi.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov's hunters, fishers and farmers struggled to feed newly freed people, which prompted the Thule offers of ilium for food. Any hunting-rights payment would be handed to the Ambassador to Otkodov.
t.Sermersuaq: Freshly reclaimed Sermersuaq faced a series of choices: completing the Jotun smokehouses and mine works, keeping, remodelling or abandoning two captured fortresses, and accepting or rejecting Thule trade and hunting proposals. A Jotun raid also threatened Kalant's roads and bridges.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Skallahn is not named on the page and is connected only through the Jotun generally.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun collapsed the pass connecting southern Sermersuaq to Skarsind.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Igya Olgafsdottir, architect of Olgafsdottirshal and Kalant, was named as the eldest child of the Jarl of Tromsa.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Wintermark can supply four armies only so long as it holds three territories and the consecrated Kallavesa Marsh.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Thule proposed a joint trading hall near Wreck in the East Floes to exchange food for ilium. They also sought hunting rights in this more populated region, and were willing to negotiate on it.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Mentioned in passing: Sealtoq is not named; it is covered only as part of Sermersuaq generally.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The bloodied Thule armies retreated to the Silver Peaks. This is where the proposed food caravans would go and where the offered ilium would come from.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Stark holds the Jotun-built Fortress of Kalant. Jarl Ragnar's force was advancing on it to destroy the surrounding roads and bridges, which would confine the garrison to defending Stark alone.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Suaq Fount's Pride of Ikka's Tears could gain 5 wains of mithril a season for 200 thrones, and 2 more through an improved route to Atalaq. The Thule also offered 15 rings of ilium to hunt in the region.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Tanikipari holds Olgafsdottirshal, the Jotun fortress some wished to rename or strip of Jotun symbols, while others wanted it kept, or decommissioned to save upkeep.

Write your own ending.d: The Seventh Wave hunted down tortured souls, Winter spirits and Druj guerrillas, so Zenith escaped lasting terror and its borders were secured. Miasma pillars still stood in Proceris, Iteri, Clypion and Lustri, denying all taxes until cleared by Senate motion or heroic stand. Sage Apollion of Tsark offered half the white granite for a Lustri fortification if the Empire swore never to enter Tsark. Prosperity priests found options to rebuild the Golden Cascade and three lost sinecures. An Autumn enchantment favoured those who moved resources to Zenith. The Senate's appraisal, led by Naomi of Virtue's Rest, proposed three follies offering Zenith a new arete. Three conjunctions dealt with tortured souls and miasma pillars.

n.Druj: Their armies were forced out of Lustri into the Sarangrave, where they were expected to resupply quickly, but their miasma pillars, tortured souls, cephalopods and lingering bands remained to torment Zenith.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's earlier warning to Tsark of an imminent Grendel attack was what persuaded Tsark to make its fortification offer.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Seventh Wave, urged on by the national assembly, rooted out the Druj legacy in Zenith. Highborn were invited to help lay tormented souls to rest at the Ring of Solace, and the proposed Radix of Truth would pay 200 herbs to Highguard's congregations for their stained glass.
n.The League: The proposed Crucible of Fate depends on finely made brass cogs from League workshops, and would bring a one-off payment of 140 ingots to League businesses if completed.
n.Urizen: Urizen regained Zenith but faced ruined spires, lost ushabti, reluctant refugees and miasma. Its assembly could endorse a new arete for the territory once one of Naomi's follies was built, and rebuilding the Golden Cascade would secure the Citadel Guard's supply.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named on this page, which concerns Zenith's restoration.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Wunderkind of Holberg are named as excelling at the precision brass work the Crucible of Fate would need.
t.Morrow: Many Zenith refugees had settled in Morrow, its senator seconded the appraisal, and surviving illuminates were founding a new spire in its south-eastern mountains. A rebuilt Golden Cascade would ease food pressures there, while losing any region of Morrow without it would see the Citadel Guard decline.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not discussed directly on this page.
t.Redoubt: Zenith refugees had put down roots in Redoubt and were reluctant to return. A rebuilt Golden Cascade would ease food pressures there, while losing any region of Redoubt without it would see the Citadel Guard decline.
t.Sarangrave: The Druj armies driven out of Lustri fled into the Sarangrave to resupply, and the proposed Citadel of the Moon would guard Zenith's border against their return.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Naomi's plan to give Zenith a new purpose was modelled on the approach used in Sarvos after the Hag Queen's curse.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: a rebuilt Golden Cascade would let Urizen supply the Citadel Guard even if it lost all access to Spiral.
t.Zenith: Liberated but devastated, Zenith remained stifled by miasma and bereft of hope. Opportunities were offered to clear the pillars, fortify Lustri, rebuild the Golden Cascade and lost sinecures, and commission a folly to define its new arete.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Mentioned in passing: the Halls of Knowledge, moved from Zenith to Peregro, were destroyed there by the Druj.
r.Zenith/Clypion: One of the four regions where Druj miasma pillars still stood, preventing any tax revenue from Zenith until they were cleared.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Miasma pillars still stood in Iteri, where the tortured souls Tibera and Gaiu were active. The region would host three of the proposed Eye of the Heavens observatories, or the Crucible of Fate at Spire Calator.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Druj were driven from Lustri, but linked miasma pillars guarded by the tortured soul Aureli Major remained. Mount Kerion was identified as the site for the proposed Citadel of the Moon.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Its miasma pillar was destroyed at the Autumn Equinox, but Druj cephalopods were infesting its lakes. The region could host restored sinecures, two observatories and the Radix of Truth, and Tormented Souls had settled in the Ring of Solace's Day regio.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris still had a miasma pillar, its waterways were infested by Druj cephalopods, and it had been flooded when the Golden Cascade was destroyed. The ruined Storm Vault there could be rebuilt alongside tempest jade workings.

You belong with me.d: After years travelling the trods with stridings, many younger Great Forest Orcs no longer wished to return to the Barrens. Corey Wayfarer proposed a mandate that would see the Great Forest Steading founded in Miaren and the High Pines Steading in Hercynia. The orcs would pay for these themselves and could be hired to boost weirwood from the Golden Trees of Seren and the Heartwood of the Great Vale. Morwenna Winterbuilt proposed a sworn oath of welcome across all Navarr territories, invoking powerful hearth magic. Cautious guides offered a mandate ending the move towards integration. With no mandate, no steadings would be founded, though the orcs might make other requests later.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs once lived under Druj dominion, and news of the Druj defeat in Zenith was met with jubilation among them.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the would-be settlers hoped to learn more about the 'orcs of the Skarsind sept', and the out-of-character note says the Imperial Orc egregore cannot bond humans.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly had to decide whether to welcome Great Forest Orc settlements beyond Therunin, a choice guides warned could lead to orcs asking to join the nation itself. An oath-sworn welcome would carry supernatural consequences if broken.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: news of the Druj defeat in Zenith was celebrated by the Great Forest Orcs.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character note cites the mora of Varushka as an example of a non-playable people.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character note cites the hylje and states the Great Forest Orcs could never join a nation so culturally unlike them as Wintermark.

t.Hercynia: Young Great Forest Orcs sought Navarr endorsement to found the permanent High Pines Steading in Hercynia, near the Heartwood of the Great Vale.
t.Miaren: A second group of young orcs sought to found the permanent Great Forest Steading in Miaren, near the Golden Trees of Seren.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the would-be settlers hoped to learn more about the 'orcs of the Skarsind sept'.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens remained the homeland most older Great Forest Orcs longed to return to, though many younger orcs now had little wish to go back there.
t.Therunin: Therunin remained the Great Forest Orcs' home-in-exile, where close bonds with their human neighbours had led some younger orcs to want to stay in the Empire permanently.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Druj defeat in Zenith was greeted with widespread jubilation among the Great Forest Orcs.

r.Hercynia/Summersend: The proposed High Pines Steading would be built in Summersend, where orc woodworkers could be hired to increase weirwood from the Heartwood of the Great Vale.
r.Miaren/Serenael: The proposed Great Forest Steading would be built in Serenael, where hired orc expertise could boost weirwood from the Golden Trees of Seren.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Senate had reassured the Great Forest Orcs of its intention to concede the Heart of Peytaht to them once the Barrens were secured, though such reassurances bind no future Senate.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Some mystically inclined Great Forest Orcs had taken up permanent residence at Peakedge Stead, studying medicinal techniques with the Navarr and Highborn.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: The orcs living in the Upper Tarn Valley had grown familiar with the Highborn of Peakedge Song and Elerael, the example the would-be settlers hoped to follow elsewhere.
